27:62.ar: أَمَّن يُجِيبُ ٱلۡمُضۡطَرَّ إِذَا دَعَاهُ وَيَكۡشِفُ ٱلسُّوٓءَ وَيَجۡعَلُكُمۡ خُلَفَآءَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ أَءِلَٰهࣱ مَّعَ ٱللَّهِۚ قَلِيلࣰ ا مَّا تَذَكَّرُونَ
27:62.en: Is not He (best) Who answereth the wronged one when he crieth unto Him and removeth the evil, and hath made you viceroys of the earth? Is there any Allah beside Allah? Little do they reflect

28:23.ar: وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ مَآءَ مَدۡيَنَ وَجَدَ عَلَيۡهِ أُمَّةࣰ مِّنَ ٱلنَّاسِ يَسۡقُونَ وَوَجَدَ مِن دُونِهِمُ ٱمۡرَأَتَيۡنِ تَذُودَانِۖ قَالَ مَا خَطۡبُكُمَاۖ قَالَتَا لَا نَسۡقِي حَتَّىٰ يُصۡدِرَ ٱلرِّعَآءُۖ وَأَبُونَا شَيۡخࣱ كَبِيرࣱ‏
28:23.en: And when he came unto the water of Midian he found there a whole tribe of men, watering. And he found apart from them two women keeping back (their flocks). He said: What aileth you? The two said: We cannot give (our flocks) to drink till the shepherds return from the water; and our father is a very old man

28:24.ar: فَسَقَىٰ لَهُمَا ثُمَّ تَوَلَّىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلظِّلِّ فَقَالَ رَبِّ إِنِّي لِمَآ أَنزَلۡتَ إِلَيَّ مِنۡ خَيۡرࣲ فَقِيرࣱ‏
28:24.en: So he watered (their flock) for them. Then he turned aside into the shade, and said: My Lord! I am needy of whatever good Thou sendest down for me

28:25.ar: فَجَآءَتۡهُ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا تَمۡشِي عَلَى ٱسۡتِحۡيَآءࣲ قَالَتۡ إِنَّ أَبِي يَدۡعُوكَ لِيَجۡزِيَكَ أَجۡرَ مَا سَقَيۡتَ لَنَاۚ فَلَمَّا جَآءَهُۥ وَقَصَّ عَلَيۡهِ ٱلۡقَصَصَ قَالَ لَا تَخَفۡۖ نَجَوۡتَ مِنَ ٱلۡقَوۡمِ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
28:25.en: Then there came unto him one of the two women, walking shyly. She said: Lo! my father biddeth thee, that he may reward thee with a payment for that thou didst water (the flock) for us. Then, when he came unto him and told him the (whole) story, he said: Fear not! Thou hast escaped from the wrongdoing folk

28:26.ar: قَالَتۡ إِحۡدَىٰهُمَا يَٰٓأَبَتِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجِرۡهُۖ إِنَّ خَيۡرَ مَنِ ٱسۡتَـٔۡجَرۡتَ ٱلۡقَوِيُّ ٱلۡأَمِينُ
28:26.en: One of the two women said: O my father! Hire him! For the best (man) that thou canst hire in the strong, the trustworthy

28:27.ar: قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أُنكِحَكَ إِحۡدَى ٱبۡنَتَيَّ هَٰتَيۡنِ عَلَىٰٓ أَن تَأۡجُرَنِي ثَمَٰنِيَ حِجَجࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَتۡمَمۡتَ عَشۡرࣰ ا فَمِنۡ عِندِكَۖ وَمَآ أُرِيدُ أَنۡ أَشُقَّ عَلَيۡكَۚ سَتَجِدُنِيٓ إِن شَآءَ ٱللَّهُ مِنَ ٱلصَّٰلِحِينَ
28:27.en: He said: Lo! I fain would marry thee to one of these two daughters of mine on condition that thou hirest thyself to me for (the term of) eight pilgrimages. Then if thou completest ten it will be of thine own accord, for I would not make it hard for thee. Allah willing, thou wilt find me of the righteous

28:59.ar: وَمَا كَانَ رَبُّكَ مُهۡلِكَ ٱلۡقُرَىٰ حَتَّىٰ يَبۡعَثَ فِيٓ أُمِّهَا رَسُولࣰ ا يَتۡلُواْ عَلَيۡهِمۡ ءَايَٰتِنَاۚ وَمَا كُنَّا مُهۡلِكِي ٱلۡقُرَىٰٓ إِلَّا وَأَهۡلُهَا ظَٰلِمُونَ
28:59.en: And never did thy Lord destroy the townships, till He had raised up in their mother(-town) a messenger reciting unto them Our revelations. And never did We destroy the townships unless the folk thereof were evil-doers

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made night everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you light? Will ye not then hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made day everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you night wherein ye rest? Will ye not then see

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: Of His mercy hath He appointed for you night and day, that therein ye may rest, and that ye may seek His bounty, and that haply ye may be thankful

28:74.ar: وَيَوۡمَ يُنَادِيهِمۡ فَيَقُولُ أَيۡنَ شُرَكَآءِيَ ٱلَّذِينَ كُنتُمۡ تَزۡعُمُونَ
28:74.en: And on the Day when He shall call unto them and say: Where are My partners whom ye pretended

28:75.ar: وَنَزَعۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةࣲ شَهِيدࣰ ا فَقُلۡنَا هَاتُواْ بُرۡهَٰنَكُمۡ فَعَلِمُوٓاْ أَنَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ لِلَّهِ وَضَلَّ عَنۡهُم مَّا كَانُواْ يَفۡتَرُونَ
28:75.en: And We shall take out from every nation a witness and We shall say: Bring your proof. Then they will know that Allah hath the Truth, and all that they invented will have failed them

29:25.ar: وَقَالَ إِنَّمَا ٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ أَوۡثَٰنࣰ ا مَّوَدَّةَ بَيۡنِكُمۡ فِي ٱلۡحَيَوٰةِ ٱلدُّنۡيَاۖ ثُمَّ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ يَكۡفُرُ بَعۡضُكُم بِبَعۡضࣲ وَيَلۡعَنُ بَعۡضُكُم بَعۡضࣰ ا وَمَأۡوَىٰكُمُ ٱلنَّارُ وَمَا لَكُم مِّن نَّٰصِرِينَ
29:25.en: He said: Ye have chosen only idols instead of Allah. The love between you is only in the life of the world. Then on the Day of Resurrection ye will deny each other and curse each other, and your abode will be the Fire, and ye will have no helpers

28:79.ar: فَخَرَجَ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمِهِۦ فِي زِينَتِهِۦۖ قَالَ ٱلَّذِينَ يُرِيدُونَ ٱلۡحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا يَٰلَيۡتَ لَنَا مِثۡلَ مَآ أُوتِيَ قَٰرُونُ إِنَّهُۥ لَذُو حَظٍّ عَظِيمࣲ‏
28:79.en: Then went he forth before his people in his pomp. Those who were desirous of the life of the world said: Ah, would that we had the like of what hath been given unto Korah! Lo! he is lord of rare good fortune

XJEisZkaENs.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; mentions sitting with terminal cancer patients and marrying at 26 after growing up in a village
XJEisZkaENs.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 19: Quranic Reflections on An-Naml 45 to Al-Ankabut 45
XJEisZkaENs.one_line: Opening the cluster on relationships: the One who answers the desperate, Musa at Madyan and healthy gender interaction, oppression's end, and idols as alliances.
XJEisZkaENs.summary: He begins the fifth cluster, about relationships. Al-Qasas concerns our relationship with people's stories: lives are simple, but what we see is easily misread, so withhold judgment. Al-Ankabut concerns our relationship with tests, an ongoing one that requires striving and sometimes leaving a comfortable state, not a wait for a smooth retirement. From An-Naml 62 he describes Allah answering the desperate, removing hardship and granting stewardship, warns against being ashamed of humble beginnings, and asks the ummah to feel the need of the oppressed in Gaza, Sudan, Kashmir and beyond. Musa at the well of Madyan asks before judging and speaks respectfully to the two women, which he uses to argue that men and women can interact with clear boundaries, criticising men who look for spouses before they are ready and urging a better, earlier path to marriage when haram is everywhere. Al-Qasas 59 teaches that Allah destroys only oppressive peoples, so any unjust nation, Muslim or not, will fall. Ibrahim's words in Al-Ankabut 25 show idolatry as a tool of alliances and power, while tawhid demands equality and merit. He closes on the witness from every nation leaving deniers with no argument.

outline.heading: The last ten nights: a chance to make up
outline.gist: Two more nights and the last third of Ramadan begins, when everything is possible and even those who did poorly can catch up. Bring your best effort and push yourself in prayer.

outline.heading: Interlude
The surahs themselves tell a story
outline.gist: Beyond each surah's verses, the sequence of their themes tells the story of what the faith is about, a level of the Quran he has loved since discovering it when young.

outline.heading: Fifth cluster: relationships; Al-Qasas and people's stories
outline.gist: The next five surahs cover our relationships. Al-Qasas is about our relationship with people and their stories: each story has someone acting and others misreading what they see.

outline.heading: Misreading Musa's mother, Musa and Qarun
outline.gist: A mother throwing her baby in the river looks terrible, Musa striking a man looks violent, Qarun looks lucky. Lives are driven by simple desires, yet we cannot read others' stories, so stop judging, assume good and move on.

outline.heading: Al-Ankabut: our relationship with tests
outline.gist: The next surah is about the tests Allah places in life, the striving they demand and sometimes hijrah, moving from one place or state to another, a lesson the companions learned early.

outline.heading: Tested by ease as well as hardship
outline.gist: Allah tests with both, but the surah dwells on difficulty because it scares us. The companions said they were tested with hardship and persevered, then with wealth, and were unsure they had been grateful.

outline.heading: Hijrah: leaving a comfortable state
outline.gist: Migration is not only Makkah to Madinah or one country to another; it can mean leaving your city, environment or friends for somewhere less comfortable in order to deal with what you face.

outline.heading: Working for a retirement that never comes
outline.gist: People work until retirement, then plan to travel the world. Sitting with someone diagnosed with terminal cancer just after retiring, he sees how an unhealthy relationship with hardship robs people of the life they deferred.

outline.heading: Hardship is an ongoing relationship
outline.gist: You cannot clear all difficulty early or postpone it. Learn to take it in stride with perseverance, striving, movement and flexibility.

outline.heading: A relationship with the world around you
outline.gist: He long wondered why this surah belongs in the cluster, then saw it: the world will keep giving good and bad until you die, and you need the right understanding of it.

outline.heading: Interlude
An-Naml: power and the spread of the message
outline.gist: These verses argue for belief from Allah's power. The strong never follow the weak; acceptance of Islam crawled for twenty years and shot up in the Prophet's last three, once Madinah had a state, an army and a proper system.

outline.heading: Is there a god with Allah?
outline.gist: Each verse ends with this rhetorical question. Amman joins 'or' and 'who': if this is not reason enough, then who else does this?

outline.heading: Who answers the one in dire need
outline.gist: The mudtarr is someone forced into a corner with no choice left, a moment everyone reaches. Who responds when he calls, if not Allah?

outline.heading: Three blessings in sequence
outline.gist: He answers the desperate, then removes the remaining harm so you reach neutral, then makes you stewards of the earth with strength. Few reflect on how He moves people between these states.

outline.heading: Forgetting the bottom of the hill
outline.gist: Once on top, people forget or hide their humble beginnings and dislike being reminded, standing by a nice car in a good suit.

outline.heading: Humble beginnings are not shameful
outline.gist: Everyone had a hard start, whether in a cloth diaper or picking change off the ground. Being ashamed of it, or forgetting it, is close to denying Allah's favour.

outline.heading: Feel the dire need of the oppressed
outline.gist: If we are one ummah we feel the desperation of Gaza, Sudan and Kashmir and of all oppressed people whatever their faith, and we call on the One who answers the desperate.

outline.heading: Other people's stories are simple
outline.gist: Lives are made of basic desires, needs, fears and hopes, like ours.

outline.heading: Simple, but not ours to judge
outline.gist: It is tempting to fill gaps and jump to conclusions. Onlookers would have thought badly of Musa's mother and of Musa shouting at a man; neither knew the story.

outline.heading: Musa reaches the water of Madyan
outline.gist: Fleeing Egypt, Musa reached the gathering at the water, where people brought their livestock to drink from a scarce resource.

outline.heading: He asked before judging
outline.gist: Seeing two women holding their sheep back among the men, he had questions about where their men were, but asked what was going on instead of judging.

outline.heading: Their answer: avoiding the crowd of men
outline.gist: They waited until the shepherds left so their flock would not mix with others and they would not be mistreated, since their father was very old. They understood his concern and answered it.

outline.heading: Musa approached them at all
outline.gist: He watered their flock and prayed. What people overlook is that he went up to two women he did not know, without any command to do so.

outline.heading: A respectful conversation in the Quran
outline.gist: Against the mentality that Muslim men and women must never speak, the Quran shows a young man and women conversing respectfully within halal limits, with no improper word or look.

outline.heading: Walking with modesty, not giggling
outline.gist: Musa became a prophet only ten years later. The daughter returning 'walking with shyness' means extreme modesty and self-respect, not the flirtatious picture he once heard someone paint.

outline.heading: Interaction with clear boundaries
outline.gist: Men and women can talk when there is need, if the boundaries are respected. Musa helped because the thirsty animals were held back, then walked away to the shade without lingering or showing off.

outline.heading: Strong and trustworthy
outline.gist: The daughter told her father he was strong and trustworthy because he made them feel completely safe. The father offered him marriage to one of his daughters because of his ethics.

outline.heading: Professional at work, on the market at the masjid
outline.gist: People who stay professional at work treat every person at Muslim gatherings as a marriage target, including a broke twenty-year-old living in his parents' basement.

outline.heading: Don't look until you are ready
outline.gist: Once you have finished studying and can support someone, knock on the door. Sisters should send him to their father; a man who cannot sit with her father is not ready.

outline.heading: The wali: a man to size up a man
outline.gist: The father judges whether a suitor will be fair, compassionate and stay through hard times. Musa walked away because, arriving from Egypt with nothing, he was not ready.

outline.heading: Do it right or not at all
outline.gist: Musa's dowry was ten years of work. Sisters should block anyone who messages unprofessionally; someone serious will do it properly.

outline.heading: A better system for marriage
outline.gist: Young people in this society have a right to access halal, so the community should remove obstacles and taboos. Not in the teens, but the early twenties seem right.

outline.heading: Haram is everywhere and marriage waits until thirty
outline.gist: In his village most men married by 23 or 24, and his friends brought children to his wedding at 26. Here haram is abundant and people wait until 30, and the community turns a blind eye.

outline.heading: The guilt that blocks being a good Muslim
outline.gist: Falling into zina for lack of access to marriage leaves hidden guilt and shame that make it hard to live as a good Muslim. The community must find a better way.

outline.heading: No punishment before a messenger
outline.gist: Allah never destroys a people before sending a messenger to their mother-town to recite His signs. We cannot say what will happen to people in the hereafter.

outline.heading: Kafir in this life; only Allah knows the next
outline.gist: In this world it is simple: you believe in Islam or you do not, and kafir is not a curse word; to people of another faith he is one too. The categories in the next life are known only to Allah.

outline.heading: Only oppressive peoples are destroyed
outline.gist: Allah punishes a people only when they are oppressors, a theme across the Quran. Any nation built on open injustice will fall, Muslim or not; the clock is ticking.

outline.heading: Why Muslim countries are in turmoil
outline.gist: They are full of oppression and will not stand until it is removed, which means removing hatred, racism and arrogance. Accept oppression on one person and you have accepted it on all.

outline.heading: No smooth sailing in life
outline.gist: Ibrahim's words belong to the surah on our relationship with difficulty, which never ends; the sooner you accept that, the better you live.

outline.heading: Live now
outline.gist: There is no promised time later, such as retirement. Find what fulfilling, meaningful living means to you and do it now.

outline.heading: Idols chosen for the bonds between you
outline.gist: Ibrahim tells his people they took idols only to build affection among themselves in this life, which proves the point he has argued for years about the purpose of idols.

outline.heading: Idols bind alliances; tawhid demands equality
outline.gist: Idols let people unite around money and power. Belief in Allah alone gives everyone the same value and the same responsibility.

outline.heading: Merit, not blood, race or wealth
outline.gist: Under tawhid status rests on effort and dedication, which the advantaged resent because they want to keep the power and wealth they hold over others.

outline.heading: Disowning each other on the Day
outline.gist: The alliances built on idols collapse at judgment when they curse one another. Polytheism persisted because it was lucrative: it let the powerful control people and pay the clergy for an idol's blessing.

outline.heading: Self-serving religion
outline.gist: Superstition and convenient rulings serve self-interest. After Ibrahim took the axe to the idols and nothing happened, he told them they knew the idols were worthless but kept them because they kept them in control.

outline.heading: Night and day as mercy
outline.gist: What if Allah made it all night or all day? The alternation is from His mercy and lets people live and function.

outline.heading: A witness from every nation: proof of concept
outline.gist: On the Day Allah will bring from every nation an example, usually its prophet, proving the teaching could be practised, and will ask them to bring their proof.

outline.heading: Their lies slip through their fingers
outline.gist: They will see that the truth was always with Allah and be left with no argument. Make sure you are not holding an argument you will lose on that Day.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The last ten nights give a second chance to anyone who fell short earlier in the month.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: People's stories are easily misread, so withhold judgment and assume the best.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Al-Ankabut frames hardship as an ongoing relationship requiring striving and sometimes hijrah, not something to clear before a comfortable retirement.

themes.label: Dua and invocation
themes.note: Allah alone answers the desperate, removes harm and grants stewardship.

themes.label: Gratitude (shukr) and appreciation
themes.note: Being ashamed of humble beginnings is close to denying Allah's favour.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The ummah should feel the desperation of Gaza, Sudan, Kashmir and all the oppressed.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Musa and the daughters of Madyan model respectful interaction with clear boundaries and modesty.

themes.label: Marriage and the relationship between spouses
themes.note: Do not look for a spouse until ready, go through the wali, and make marriage easier and earlier in a society where haram is everywhere.

themes.label: Justice and refusing oppression
themes.note: Allah destroys only oppressive peoples; Muslim countries will not stand until oppression, racism and arrogance are removed.

themes.label: Human equality and racism
themes.note: Tawhid demands equal value and responsibility and status by merit, which is why the privileged cling to idols.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Each nation's witness will leave the deniers with no argument on the Day of Judgment.

quran.point: Onlookers called Qarun lucky, an example of misreading someone's story.

hadith.gist: The companions said they were tested with hardship and were patient, then tested with ease and were not sure they had been grateful.

maxims: People's stories are simple, but not ours to judge
The strong never follow the weak
Accept oppression on one and you've accepted it on all
If he can't sit with your father, he isn't ready
Live now

stories.who: A patient given a terminal diagnosis just after retiring
stories.point: Postponing life until hardship ends is an unhealthy relationship with the world.

stories.who: Musa at the well of Madyan
stories.point: Ask before judging, help where needed, keep clear boundaries, and do not pursue marriage before you are ready.

stories.who: His village friends who married in their early twenties
stories.point: Delaying marriage to thirty in a society full of haram harms young people and the community.

stories.who: Ibrahim confronting his people over their idols
stories.point: Idolatry serves alliances and power; tawhid demands equality.

contemporary: The suffering of people in Gaza, Sudan and Kashmir
Western retirement culture of working until retirement and only then living
Marriage delayed to the thirties in Western Muslim communities while haram is easily available
Young Muslims treating community gatherings as a marriage market and messaging unprofessionally
Oppression, racism and turmoil in Muslim-majority countries
takeaways: Do not judge people from what you see of their lives; ask before assuming, as Musa did.
Remember your humble beginnings and call on Allah for the oppressed whose need you should feel as your own.
Young men should not look for a spouse until ready and should go through the woman's father; sisters should block unprofessional approaches; communities should make marriage easier.
Reject oppression, racism and arrogance among Muslims, since oppressive nations fall.
Live a meaningful life now instead of waiting for a hardship-free future.

23:14.ar: ثُمَّ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلنُّطۡفَةَ عَلَقَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡعَلَقَةَ مُضۡغَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمُضۡغَةَ عِظَٰمࣰ ا فَكَسَوۡنَا ٱلۡعِظَٰمَ لَحۡمࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَٰهُ خَلۡقًا ءَاخَرَۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقِينَ
23:14.en: Then fashioned We the drop a clot, then fashioned We the clot a little lump, then fashioned We the little lump bones, then clothed the bones with flesh, and then produced it as another creation. So blessed be Allah, the Best of creators

23:36.en: Begone, begone, with that which ye are promised

23:99.ar: حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَهُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ قَالَ رَبِّ ٱرۡجِعُونِ
23:99.en: Until, when death cometh unto one of them, he saith: My Lord! Send me back

23:100.ar: لَعَلِّيٓ أَعۡمَلُ صَٰلِحࣰ ا فِيمَا تَرَكۡتُۚ كَلَّآۚ إِنَّهَا كَلِمَةٌ هُوَ قَآئِلُهَاۖ وَمِن وَرَآئِهِم بَرۡزَخٌ إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ يُبۡعَثُونَ
23:100.en: That I may do right in that which I have left behind! But nay! It is but a word that he speaketh; and behind them is a barrier until the day when they are raised

24:15.ar: إِذۡ تَلَقَّوۡنَهُۥ بِأَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَتَقُولُونَ بِأَفۡوَاهِكُم مَّا لَيۡسَ لَكُم بِهِۦ عِلۡمࣱ وَتَحۡسَبُونَهُۥ هَيِّنࣰ ا وَهُوَ عِندَ ٱللَّهِ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:15.en: When ye welcomed it with your tongues, and uttered with your mouths that whereof ye had no knowledge, ye counted it a trifle. In the sight of Allah it is very great

24:16.ar: وَلَوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ قُلۡتُم مَّا يَكُونُ لَنَآ أَن نَّتَكَلَّمَ بِهَٰذَا سُبۡحَٰنَكَ هَٰذَا بُهۡتَٰنٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
24:16.en: Wherefor, when ye heard it, said ye not: It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to Thee (O Allah)! This is awful calumny

24:17.ar: يَعِظُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ أَن تَعُودُواْ لِمِثۡلِهِۦٓ أَبَدًا إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
24:17.en: Allah admonisheth you that ye repeat not the like thereof ever, if ye are (in truth) believers

24:26.ar: ٱلۡخَبِيثَٰتُ لِلۡخَبِيثِينَ وَٱلۡخَبِيثُونَ لِلۡخَبِيثَٰتِۖ وَٱلطَّيِّبَٰتُ لِلطَّيِّبِينَ وَٱلطَّيِّبُونَ لِلطَّيِّبَٰتِۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مُبَرَّءُونَ مِمَّا يَقُولُونَۖ لَهُم مَّغۡفِرَةࣱ وَرِزۡقࣱ كَرِيمࣱ‏
24:26.en: Vile women are for vile men, and vile men for vile women. Good women are for good men, and good men for good women; such are innocent of that which people say: For them is pardon and a bountiful provision

24:40.ar: أَوۡ كَظُلُمَٰتࣲ فِي بَحۡرࣲ لُّجِّيࣲّ يَغۡشَىٰهُ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ مَوۡجࣱ مِّن فَوۡقِهِۦ سَحَابࣱۚ ظُلُمَٰتُۢ بَعۡضُهَا فَوۡقَ بَعۡضٍ إِذَآ أَخۡرَجَ يَدَهُۥ لَمۡ يَكَدۡ يَرَىٰهَاۗ وَمَن لَّمۡ يَجۡعَلِ ٱللَّهُ لَهُۥ نُورࣰ ا فَمَا لَهُۥ مِن نُّورٍ
24:40.en: Or as darkness on a vast, abysmal sea. There covereth him a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud. Layer upon layer of darkness. When he holdeth out his hand he scarce can see it. And he for whom Allah hath not appointed light, for him there is no light

24:4.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَرۡمُونَ ٱلۡمُحۡصَنَٰتِ ثُمَّ لَمۡ يَأۡتُواْ بِأَرۡبَعَةِ شُهَدَآءَ فَٱجۡلِدُوهُمۡ ثَمَٰنِينَ جَلۡدَةࣰ وَلَا تَقۡبَلُواْ لَهُمۡ شَهَٰدَةً أَبَدࣰ اۚ وَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ هُمُ ٱلۡفَٰسِقُونَ
24:4.en: And those who accuse honourable women but bring not four witnesses, scourge them (with) eighty stripes and never (afterward) accept their testimony - They indeed are evil-doers

24:12.ar: لَّوۡلَآ إِذۡ سَمِعۡتُمُوهُ ظَنَّ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ وَٱلۡمُؤۡمِنَٰتُ بِأَنفُسِهِمۡ خَيۡرࣰ ا وَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِفۡكࣱ مُّبِينࣱ‏
24:12.en: Why did not the believers, men and women, when ye heard it, think good of their own own folk, and say: It is a manifest untruth

24:35.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ نُورُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ مَثَلُ نُورِهِۦ كَمِشۡكَوٰةࣲ فِيهَا مِصۡبَاحٌۖ ٱلۡمِصۡبَاحُ فِي زُجَاجَةٍۖ ٱلزُّجَاجَةُ كَأَنَّهَا كَوۡكَبࣱ دُرِّيࣱّ يُوقَدُ مِن شَجَرَةࣲ مُّبَٰرَكَةࣲ زَيۡتُونَةࣲ لَّا شَرۡقِيَّةࣲ وَلَا غَرۡبِيَّةࣲ يَكَادُ زَيۡتُهَا يُضِيٓءُ وَلَوۡ لَمۡ تَمۡسَسۡهُ نَارࣱۚ نُّورٌ عَلَىٰ نُورࣲۚ يَهۡدِي ٱللَّهُ لِنُورِهِۦ مَن يَشَآءُۚ وَيَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَٰلَ لِلنَّاسِۗ وَٱللَّهُ بِكُلِّ شَيۡءٍ عَلِيمࣱ‏
24:35.en: Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The similitude of His light is as a niche wherein is a lamp. The lamp is in a glass. The glass is as it were a shining star. (This lamp is) kindled from a blessed tree, an olive neither of the East nor of the West, whose oil would almost glow forth (of itself) though no fire touched it. Light upon light. Allah guideth unto His light whom He will. And Allah speaketh to mankind in allegories, for Allah is Knower of all things

RlnXaNrboPI.speaker: adnan
RlnXaNrboPI.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; critiques the organisational focus of London's Muslim community
RlnXaNrboPI.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 17: Quranic Reflections on Al-Hajj 58 to An-Nur 64
RlnXaNrboPI.one_line: Investing in people over buildings, the embryo's stages, belief in resurrection, death's plea to return, rumours and social media, and Allah's light.
RlnXaNrboPI.summary: He reads Al-Hajj as framing the message as a demanding journey, then argues from Al-Muminun that the message's real value is people, criticising communities, London included, that pour effort into buildings and numbers instead of mentoring youth. An-Nur adds that only an enlightened community, protected from the pitfalls of collective behaviour, can carry the message and attract others. Al-Muminun 14 shows Allah's precise knowledge in the stages of the embryo. Al-Muminun 36 voices the deniers' 'far, far away', and he argues that most Muslims believe in resurrection only halfway; real certainty would change daily choices. Verses 99-100 describe the dying person begging to return, and he stresses that death is the most certain thing ahead. On An-Nur 15 and the slander of Aisha, he explains Islam's protection of a woman's honour and condemns those who pass on rumours they claim not to believe, then warns that social media makes such harm instant and permanent, urging parents not to give young children phones. He corrects a common misreading of An-Nur 26 about marriage, warning that it shuts out the repentant, and closes on the darkness of those to whom Allah gives no light.

outline.heading: Opening
Al-Hajj: the pilgrimage as an analogy for the message
outline.gist: Al-Hajj presents carrying the message as a journey, and Hajj itself gains a new dimension once you see the parallel: it demands perseverance, flexibility, commitment and striving.

outline.heading: Absorbing hardship for a bigger purpose
outline.gist: Beyond the history of Ibrahim and Muhammad at the sites, Hajj means days of crowds and exhaustion among people who break the rules or came for the wrong reasons. You absorb it all because you have a bigger goal, just as in carrying the message.

outline.heading: Al-Muminun: the value of the message is people
outline.gist: The surah lists the attributes of those who carry the message and makes the human being, not anything else, the true value to invest in.

outline.heading: Buildings over people
outline.gist: Muslim communities in the West and back home overemphasise spaces and architecture while barely investing in educating, mentoring and empowering youth to build identity and take responsibility.

outline.heading: The organisational problem in London
outline.gist: The focus is on how many places there are, how big and fancy, how many cars they hold, or whether the imam has a nice voice. A beautiful recitation was never the point; it is superficial to dwell on it.

outline.heading: A full masjid proves nothing
outline.gist: People attend the nearest masjid anyway. The question is whether there is investment in those leading the work and in the youth coming in, listening to where they are and helping them on their journey.

outline.heading: An-Nur: an enlightened, pious community
outline.gist: A community with the right values becomes enlightened, with light in it rather than darkness, and the surah gives examples of how communities should behave.

outline.heading: The pitfalls of collective behaviour
outline.gist: Groups fall into different traps than individuals, and understanding the difference is key. A community lacking enlightened values is not qualified to carry the message.

outline.heading: The world needs an enlightened community as an example
outline.gist: An impressive individual Muslim proves little, since every faith has impressive people. What turns heads is a whole society protected from corruption by its faith, and people will change their lives for that.

outline.heading: See a person, not a dollar bill
outline.gist: When someone walks into the masjid, communities should see a person to teach, mentor and empower as the next in line to carry the deen.

outline.heading: Interlude
A glimpse of the precision of Allah's knowledge
outline.gist: The verse traces the stages of the embryo, something people only began to understand many centuries after the Prophet.

outline.heading: Nutfah to alaqah: the clinging stage
outline.gist: The fertilised egg divides quickly and some cells take on the job of holding on to the uterine wall; if they fail to cling, there is an early miscarriage most women never notice.

outline.heading: Mudghah: what looks chewed
outline.gist: The early spine looks as if someone bit into it, as cells migrate and form the indentation that begins the spinal cord.

outline.heading: Bones, flesh, then another creation
outline.gist: Bones differentiate and are covered with flesh, then the tiny form grows into something entirely different: what you become.

outline.heading: The companion who said it before revelation
outline.gist: A companion listening to the Prophet recite these stages exclaimed 'blessed is Allah, the best of creators' from his grasp of the language, before that ending had been revealed.

outline.heading: 'Best of creators' when only He creates
outline.gist: Strictly only Allah brings things from nothing, but creation also means producing something new from existing elements, as in English. No one creates better than Him.

outline.heading: A generic prophet story after Nuh
outline.gist: The second story in the surah names no prophet; scholars differ on who it is. It is the common skeleton of every prophet's story: evidence, preaching, rejection.

outline.heading: First objection: a human messenger
outline.gist: People find it hard to follow a human being just like themselves.

outline.heading: Second objection: rules and prohibitions
outline.gist: People dislike being told what they must and must not do.

outline.heading: Third objection: resurrection and accountability
outline.gist: People do not want to be raised from the earth after death and held accountable for their choices.

outline.heading: Hayhat, hayhat: far, far away
outline.gist: Hayhat, still used in Levantine Arabic, means it is not going to happen. Saying it twice makes resurrection seem so unlikely it is not worth believing: there is only this life.

outline.heading: If people truly believed, they would live differently
outline.gist: Real belief in accountability before Allah alone, with every choice recorded, makes it impossible to waste time or wealth, harm others or eat haram.

outline.heading: We kind of believe it, but not really
outline.gist: Our failures come from half-belief in resurrection. The believer takes it as fact: we will come out of our graves, be held accountable and sent one of two ways.

outline.heading: Remove resurrection and the equation of life collapses
outline.gist: Without certainty in it, nothing makes sense, not even fasting for thirty days. Treating it as far-fetched led the deniers to choices they regretted.

outline.heading: When death comes to one of them
outline.gist: Among the most beautiful verses: death comes to you, and even when people seek it, it is still decreed.

outline.heading: Every person in this room will die
outline.gist: As the spirit is drawn out and control slips away, reality changes. This will happen to everyone; it is only a matter of time, and every hour brings us closer.

outline.heading: Nothing is more certain than your death
outline.gist: You may have successes and achievements ahead, but the one thing you are heading toward without question is the end of your life.

outline.heading: 'My Lord, send me back'
outline.gist: The first words are a plea to return and do better now that it makes sense. Allah answers that they will never go back; it is only a word they say, and ahead lies the barzakh until resurrection.

outline.heading: The slander of Aisha
outline.gist: Aisha and Safwan were accused of something they never did and the rumour spread through Madinah. An-Nur first sets the rules on zina, then turns to how a community must treat such talk.

outline.heading: A woman's honour has its own category
outline.gist: Islam values human dignity and especially a woman's integrity. Gossip has several names, but accusing a woman's chastity, qadhf, is its own category with its own punishment.

outline.heading: Publicly lashed for an unproven accusation
outline.gist: Accusing a man may lead to a lawsuit or a public apology; accusing a woman without proof can bring public lashing.

outline.heading: First group: those who denied it
outline.gist: Without four witnesses who saw it in the open, not by peeking, there is no case, and private sins, though haram, are not publicly punished. A Muslim's duty is to reject the accusation outright without needing evidence, because we conceal people's sins.

outline.heading: Second group: those who stayed silent
outline.gist: Silence was not good enough; they should have spoken up.

outline.heading: The fabricators: beyond the surah's address
outline.gist: Those who invented the rumour face Allah's curse and the Fire; the surah does not even address them.

outline.heading: Third group: 'I don't believe it, but...'
outline.gist: Some passed it on without believing it, taking it from tongue to tongue and speaking of what they had no knowledge of.

outline.heading: You think it trivial; to Allah it is grave
outline.gist: 'I'm just sharing information' feels harmless, but ask how you would feel if someone spread a rumour about you while claiming not to believe it. It is your reputation and your life.

outline.heading: Never return to it, if you are believers
outline.gist: Allah warns them never to repeat this. Social media has potential for good, but it is hard to praise given how much garbage and harm it carries.

outline.heading: Cause no harm: rumours at the speed of a post
outline.gist: One act of harm can ruin a legacy of good, and avoiding harm is the first rule in Islam as in medicine. A rumour that once passed to a few people now reaches a million in minutes and can never be deleted.

outline.heading: Young people and phones
outline.gist: He disagrees with parents giving phones to children who do not need them. It is unfair that a seventeen-year-old's mistake should never be forgotten; the young must be able to make mistakes that wash off.

outline.heading: Mistakes that haunt a person for life
outline.gist: A post or video can force someone to move or change their name and damage their ability to grow. He sees more immaturity, not more wisdom, in how phones are used.

outline.heading: A thumb's movement away from lasting harm
outline.gist: Islam keeps people far from harm so that their mistakes still land far from it. Phones put permanent, staining harm one wrong movement away, which is too close, especially for the young.

outline.heading: Not about who marries whom
outline.gist: The verse does not mean good men marry good women and bad marry bad. Bad deeds belong to bad people and good deeds to good people, and each seeks out its own.

outline.heading: A misreading that shuts out the repentant
outline.gist: Still seek a pious spouse, but using this verse to say people with a repented past can never marry someone good creates two societies that never mix and denies repentance.

outline.heading: The parable of darkness in a deep sea
outline.gist: After the parables of Allah's light granted to communities that follow Him, He gives the image of darkness in a raging sea, wave upon wave, beneath dark clouds.

outline.heading: Layers of darkness: unable to see your own hand
outline.gist: A community can sink into such darkness that it cannot see what is right in front of it, and we are not immune.

outline.heading: Whomever Allah gives no light has no light
outline.gist: The light in our lives is only what Allah grants, which is why we come asking Him for it; without it, there is no light at all.

themes.label: Hajj, Umrah and Arafah
themes.note: Hajj's crowds and hardships mirror the demands of carrying the message, giving the pilgrimage a new dimension.

themes.label: Community building, cooperation and the ummah
themes.note: The message's value is people; communities must invest in mentoring youth rather than buildings and numbers, and become enlightened examples.

themes.label: The masjid: its role and etiquette
themes.note: In London the focus falls on the size and number of buildings and the imam's voice, while a full masjid proves nothing.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: The stages of the embryo show the precision of Allah's knowledge, the best of creators.

themes.label: Accountability before Allah and goals
themes.note: Half-belief in resurrection explains our failures; true certainty in accountability changes daily choices.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death is the most certain thing ahead; the dying beg to return and are refused.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: From the slander of Aisha: reject unproven accusations, never stay silent, and never pass on rumours even while claiming not to believe them.

themes.label: Gender relations, chastity and modesty
themes.note: Islam gives a woman's honour special protection, making unproven accusation against her a punishable offence.

themes.label: Technology, AI, social media and attention
themes.note: Social media spreads harm instantly and permanently; children should not have phones they do not need.

themes.label: The unlawfulness of harm and protecting others
themes.note: Causing no harm is the first rule, and Islam keeps people far from harm so their mistakes stay recoverable.

themes.label: Tawbah: repentance and returning to Allah
themes.note: Misreading 24:26 to exclude the repentant from good marriages denies repentance its place in society.

themes.label: Guidance (hidayah)
themes.note: Light comes only from Allah; communities without it cannot see what is in front of them.

quran.point: The punishment of lashing for accusing a chaste woman without four witnesses.
The believers should have thought well and called it an obvious lie.
The parable of Allah's light that precedes the parable of darkness.

hadith.gist: A companion hearing the Prophet recite the stages of creation exclaimed 'blessed is Allah, the best of creators', and the verse was revealed ending with those words.
The slander against Aisha that spread through Madinah until revelation cleared her.
The principle that there is to be no harm and no reciprocating harm.

maxims: The value of this message is people
You see a person, not a dollar bill
We kind of believe in it, but not really
Stay far from harm so your mistakes stay far from it

stories.who: The companion who anticipated the end of 23:14
stories.point: Purity of language let him reach the verse's conclusion before it was revealed.

stories.who: The unnamed prophet of Al-Muminun
stories.point: Every prophet's story shares the same skeleton, and rejection of resurrection led people to choices they regretted.

stories.who: The slander of Aisha (al-ifk)
stories.point: A community must reject unproven accusations; staying silent or passing them on is a grave wrong.

contemporary: London's Muslim institutions focusing on buildings, size and the imam's voice rather than investing in people
Social media spreading rumours to millions within minutes and making mistakes permanent
Parents giving phones to young children and teens who do not need them
The common misuse of An-Nur 26 to judge marriages and exclude people with a repented past
takeaways: Invest in people, especially youth, through mentoring and education, rather than in buildings and attendance numbers.
Let real certainty in resurrection and accountability shape daily choices about time, wealth and halal.
Reject unproven accusations outright and never pass on a rumour, even while saying you do not believe it.
Do not give young children phones they do not need, and be careful what you post.
Do not use An-Nur 26 to shut repentant people out of good marriages.

29:51.ar: أَوَلَمۡ يَكۡفِهِمۡ أَنَّآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ يُتۡلَىٰ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَرَحۡمَةࣰ وَذِكۡرَىٰ لِقَوۡمࣲ يُؤۡمِنُونَ
29:51.en: Is it not enough for them that We have sent down unto thee the Scripture which is read unto them? Lo! herein verily is mercy, and a reminder for folk who believe

30:22.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦ خَلۡقُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱخۡتِلَٰفُ أَلۡسِنَتِكُمۡ وَأَلۡوَٰنِكُمۡۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّلۡعَٰلِمِينَ
30:22.en: And of His signs is the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the difference of your languages and colours. Lo! herein indeed are portents for men of knowledge

30:50.ar: فَٱنظُرۡ إِلَىٰٓ ءَاثَٰرِ رَحۡمَتِ ٱللَّهِ كَيۡفَ يُحۡيِ ٱلۡأَرۡضَ بَعۡدَ مَوۡتِهَآۚ إِنَّ ذَٰلِكَ لَمُحۡيِ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
30:50.en: Look, therefore, at the prints of Allah's mercy (in creation): how He quickeneth the earth after her death. Lo! He verily is the Quickener of the Dead, and He is Able to do all things

31:27.ar: وَلَوۡ أَنَّمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مِن شَجَرَةٍ أَقۡلَٰمࣱ وَٱلۡبَحۡرُ يَمُدُّهُۥ مِنۢ بَعۡدِهِۦ سَبۡعَةُ أَبۡحُرࣲ مَّا نَفِدَتۡ كَلِمَٰتُ ٱللَّهِۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ حَكِيمࣱ‏
31:27.en: And if all the trees in the earth were pens, and the sea, with seven more seas to help it, (were ink), the words of Allah could not be exhausted. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Wise

32:16.ar: تَتَجَافَىٰ جُنُوبُهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلۡمَضَاجِعِ يَدۡعُونَ رَبَّهُمۡ خَوۡفࣰ ا وَطَمَعࣰ ا وَمِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ يُنفِقُونَ
32:16.en: Who forsake their beds to cry unto their Lord in fear and hope, and spend of that We have bestowed on them

33:23.ar: مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ رِجَالࣱ صَدَقُواْ مَا عَٰهَدُواْ ٱللَّهَ عَلَيۡهِۖ فَمِنۡهُم مَّن قَضَىٰ نَحۡبَهُۥ وَمِنۡهُم مَّن يَنتَظِرُۖ وَمَا بَدَّلُواْ تَبۡدِيلࣰ ا
33:23.en: Of the believers are men who are true to that which they covenanted with Allah. Some of them have paid their vow by death (in battle), and some of them still are waiting; and they have not altered in the least

30:54.ar: ۞ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُم مِّن ضَعۡفࣲ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ ضَعۡفࣲ قُوَّةࣰ ثُمَّ جَعَلَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ قُوَّةࣲ ضَعۡفࣰ ا وَشَيۡبَةࣰۚ يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡقَدِيرُ
30:54.en: Allah is He Who shaped you out of weakness, then appointed after weakness strength, then, after strength, appointed weakness and grey hair. He createth what He will. He is the Knower, the Mighty

30:3.ar: فِيٓ أَدۡنَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَهُم مِّنۢ بَعۡدِ غَلَبِهِمۡ سَيَغۡلِبُونَ
30:3.en: In the nearer land, and they, after their defeat will be victorious

30:4.ar: فِي بِضۡعِ سِنِينَۗ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡأَمۡرُ مِن قَبۡلُ وَمِنۢ بَعۡدُۚ وَيَوۡمَئِذࣲ يَفۡرَحُ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنُونَ
30:4.en: Within ten years - Allah's is the command in the former case and in the latter - and in that day believers will rejoice

54:1.en: The hour drew nigh and the moon was rent in twain

30:21.ar: وَمِنۡ ءَايَٰتِهِۦٓ أَنۡ خَلَقَ لَكُم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِكُمۡ أَزۡوَٰجࣰ ا لِّتَسۡكُنُوٓاْ إِلَيۡهَا وَجَعَلَ بَيۡنَكُم مَّوَدَّةࣰ وَرَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّ فِي ذَٰلِكَ لَأٓيَٰتࣲ لِّقَوۡمࣲ يَتَفَكَّرُونَ
30:21.en: And of His signs is this: He created for you helpmeets from yourselves that ye might find rest in them, and He ordained between you love and mercy. Lo! herein indeed are portents for folk who reflect

9:111.ar: ۞إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ ٱشۡتَرَىٰ مِنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ أَنفُسَهُمۡ وَأَمۡوَٰلَهُم بِأَنَّ لَهُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةَۚ يُقَٰتِلُونَ فِي سَبِيلِ ٱللَّهِ فَيَقۡتُلُونَ وَيُقۡتَلُونَۖ وَعۡدًا عَلَيۡهِ حَقࣰّ ا فِي ٱلتَّوۡرَىٰةِ وَٱلۡإِنجِيلِ وَٱلۡقُرۡءَانِۚ وَمَنۡ أَوۡفَىٰ بِعَهۡدِهِۦ مِنَ ٱللَّهِۚ فَٱسۡتَبۡشِرُواْ بِبَيۡعِكُمُ ٱلَّذِي بَايَعۡتُم بِهِۦۚ وَذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡفَوۡزُ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
9:111.en: Lo! Allah hath bought from the believers their lives and their wealth because the Garden will be theirs: they shall fight in the way of Allah and shall slay and be slain. It is a promise which is binding on Him in the Torah and the Gospel and the Qur'an. Who fulfilleth His covenant better than Allah? Rejoice then in your bargain that ye have made, for that is the supreme triumph

4:69.ar: وَمَن يُطِعِ ٱللَّهَ وَٱلرَّسُولَ فَأُوْلَٰٓئِكَ مَعَ ٱلَّذِينَ أَنۡعَمَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡهِم مِّنَ ٱلنَّبِيِّـۧنَ وَٱلصِّدِّيقِينَ وَٱلشُّهَدَآءِ وَٱلصَّٰلِحِينَۚ وَحَسُنَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ رَفِيقࣰ ا
4:69.en: Whoso obeyeth Allah and the messenger, they are with those unto whom Allah hath shown favour, of the prophets and the saints and the martyrs and the righteous. The best of company are they

EWGGU5yeJ34.speaker: adnan
EWGGU5yeJ34.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; recounts his teachers back home objecting to his English khutbahs
EWGGU5yeJ34.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 20: Quranic Reflections on Al-Ankabut 46 to Al-Ahzab 35
EWGGU5yeJ34.one_line: Relationships with Allah's laws, across generations and with Allah Himself: the Quran is enough, diversity is a sign, and being true to the covenant.
EWGGU5yeJ34.summary: He completes the cluster on relationships. Ar-Rum is about our relationship with Allah's laws in the world: unity and justice bring strength, their absence brings defeat, and the stages of weakness, strength and weakness mean you should use your strength for Allah now. Luqman is about relationships between generations: the young should listen to elders' experience and the old should train and empower the young, as the Prophet did effortlessly with companions like Anas. As-Sajdah is about our relationship with Allah, which, like any relationship, grows dull without investment. On Al-Ankabut 51 he argues the Quran is enough and the Prophet's only challenge, unlike other wonders. Ar-Rum 22 makes diversity of languages and races a sign to celebrate; Islam does not erase cultures or Arabize people, though Muslims should learn Arabic to read the Quran directly. Ar-Rum 50 links reviving dead earth to resurrection, and Luqman 27 shows Allah's endless wisdom and the wisdom around us in our elders. As-Sajdah 16 describes believers who cannot stay in bed for longing to pray at night. Al-Ahzab 23 praises those true to their covenant; he distinguishes dying for Allah from living for Him and honours Palestinians who refuse to leave their land.

outline.heading: When the last ten nights begin
outline.gist: Some scholars count tonight as the first of the last ten, and the Hanafis reach back further, but the stronger view divides the month into tens starting from the twenty-first night.

outline.heading: Interlude
Ramadan cascades to its end
outline.gist: The month ends before we feel it, and no one knows if they will see another; he prays for many more.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recap: relationships with people and with life
outline.gist: Al-Qasas covered our relationship with people's stories and Al-Ankabut our ongoing relationship with life's ease and difficulty, which must be mastered through striving and perseverance.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum: our relationship with Allah's laws
outline.gist: Allah's laws govern change, power, wealth and communities. The law says a united and just people will be strong and a divided, unjust one will lose; when we ask why things are not better, the ball is in our court.

outline.heading: No swimming against the tide
outline.gist: A prosperous nation needs unity, power, knowledge, wealth and resources. Allah will not break His laws for us; He demands that we live by them.

outline.heading: Weakness, strength, weakness: use your strength now
outline.gist: Allah created you from weakness, then gave strength, then weakness again. Postponing devotion until you are weak works against the law: memorising Quran at thirteen is far easier than at thirty, and learning Islam in your twenties easier than in your forties. The surah opens with the Romans' defeat and later victory.

outline.heading: Luqman: relationships between generations
outline.gist: The surah summarises cross-generational ties in Luqman's advice to his son; failing to use these relationships loses a great deal.

outline.heading: Listen first, then lead
outline.gist: The previous generation did some things well and others badly; before fighting the world, listen to what they offer. Young people can lead instead of leaders in their seventies, but only if elders feel respected and the young are coached, trained and empowered alongside experience.

outline.heading: The Prophet as a master of empowering youth
outline.gist: He made everyone, especially the young, feel valuable and heard, put them in positions, watched, gave feedback and gave them another chance, as a side task while running a nation.

outline.heading: A generation that carried his legacy
outline.gist: Those he empowered could not bear life without him and spread his legacy, which is why we are here. Anas, a ten-year-old in his household, taught into his late nineties, and Abu Hanifah is reported to have met him.

outline.heading: As-Sajdah: every relationship can grow dull
outline.gist: Friendships and marriages fall into routine until there is little left to say, and even silence, which he finds underrated, can signal a fading spark.

outline.heading: Your relationship with Allah is no different
outline.gist: Without effort to ignite it, worship becomes boring; some people pray as if it were torture.

outline.heading: Sides that cannot stay in bed
outline.gist: Believers are so eager to stand before Allah they cannot keep still in bed, calling on Him in fear and hope. That longing takes work to build and nurture.

outline.heading: Why As-Sajdah is recited every Friday dawn
outline.gist: The most important relationship is the reason the surah is read at Fajr on Fridays almost everywhere, a day surrounded by rituals because of its importance.

outline.heading: Interlude
Sixth cluster: obedience when it is hard
outline.gist: The next cluster, starting with Al-Ahzab, covers submission to Allah specifically when it is difficult, whether physically, financially, socially, reputationally or psychologically.

outline.heading: Where are his miracles?
outline.gist: People asked why the Prophet had no physical miracles like earlier prophets, such as Salih's she-camel.

outline.heading: Is the Book not enough?
outline.gist: The answer is yes: the recited Quran holds mercy and reminders for believers. Allah never opens a door to guidance without giving the tools to walk through it, and the Quran is always on the shelf.

outline.heading: Our craving for wonders
outline.gist: People reach for more, such as the splitting of the moon, which if it happened was seen by few and happened once, unlike Musa's staff shown again and again. He holds that the verse in Al-Qamar is not about that event.

outline.heading: Signs of baraka versus the one challenge
outline.gist: Food multiplying in his hands happened as blessing and signs of prophethood, but he never challenged anyone with them. His only challenge was the Quran, which the Arabs could not match.

outline.heading: Ar-Rum counts Allah's signs
outline.gist: In a surah about Allah's laws, He lists His signs; the verse just before is recited at nearly every Muslim wedding.

outline.heading: Alwan: races, cultures and backgrounds
outline.gist: Alongside the heavens and earth, the diversity of tongues and colours is a sign. Lawn means kinds or types, so the verse speaks of races, cultures and backgrounds.

outline.heading: Diversity is a sign to celebrate
outline.gist: Seeing different peoples should draw the same 'subhan Allah' as seeing the cosmos. Islam was never meant to erase cultures or Arabize people.

outline.heading: Keep the good in your culture, learn the Quran's tongue
outline.gist: The Quran affirms what is good in a culture and removes what is not, and asks people to keep their language while learning Arabic to understand it. He finds it strange to be speaking English to his community at all.

outline.heading: Ripped apart for preaching in English
outline.gist: He learned Islam entirely in Arabic and has read no Islamic books in English. When his teacher found one of his khutbahs and shared it with senior scholars, they tore into him for speaking English from the minbar.

outline.heading: Learn Arabic so no one stands between you and the Book
outline.gist: Islam does not erase your tongue, but Arabic gives you direct access to what Allah says without a middle person. Diversity is only positive.

outline.heading: Eid garments and signs for those who know
outline.gist: He loves the outdoor Eid prayer where everyone comes in their cultural dress. Islam only removes what is harmful or haram. One reading ends the verse with 'for people of knowledge', another 'for all people'.

outline.heading: Look at the traces of Allah's mercy
outline.gist: Allah tells us to look at the effects of His mercy in the world.

outline.heading: Dead earth revived, and the dead raised
outline.gist: He gives life to dead land, and the same ability will resurrect the dead. The verse is a celebration of His mercy.

outline.heading: Interlude
All trees as pens and the ocean as ink
outline.gist: In the commentary after Luqman's advice: if every tree were a pen and the ocean ink, replenished by seven more oceans.

outline.heading: Seven means infinity: His words never run out
outline.gist: Seven signals endlessness, like the week that restarts. With infinite ink, Allah's knowledge and wisdom would still not be exhausted.

outline.heading: Wisdom is all around you
outline.gist: In a surah on generational ties: Allah's wisdom is infinite, but there is wisdom near you. Listen to parents, grandparents and those who have lived; that is how you win time.

outline.heading: Wisdom comes from experience, not books
outline.gist: Young people may have read more than their parents, but they have not lived long enough to have more wisdom.

outline.heading: The most valuable relationship of all
outline.gist: As-Sajdah ends the cluster with our relationship with Allah.

outline.heading: Relationships you don't invest in die
outline.gist: Friends, relatives, spouses, children and parents: neglected relationships become empty burdens where every conversation opens old conflicts.

outline.heading: Struggling with salah means no relationship yet
outline.gist: Invest your time and heart in Allah or the relationship loses meaning and people drift. Once it is real, you would be fine dropped anywhere in time or place.

outline.heading: Tatajafa: sides that shun their beds
outline.gist: Imams recite this verse almost everywhere on Friday mornings. Tajafi means avoiding contact, giving the cold shoulder: their sides refuse the mattress.

outline.heading: Too excited to sit still
outline.gist: They call their Lord in fear and hope and spend from what He gave. The phrase captures the restlessness of a child awaiting something exciting.

outline.heading: The King calls in the last part of the night
outline.gist: You can have that passion with Allah: knowing He descends to the lowest heaven asking who will call, seek forgiveness and ask, you cannot stay in bed.

outline.heading: The Prophet waiting for Aisha to sleep
outline.gist: He would lie waiting for his wife to fall asleep so he could rise to pray without disturbing her, and once asked her leave to go and pray. That is a relationship worth having.

outline.heading: Al-Ahzab: obedience through every kind of hardship
outline.gist: The longest surah of its cluster covers about six kinds of difficulty, opening with the Battle of the Trench, and later looks back on those who stood firm.

outline.heading: True to the covenant: lives sold for Jannah
outline.gist: The covenant is that Allah bought the believers' lives and wealth in exchange for Paradise. Some were truthful to it and have died; others still wait their turn.

outline.heading: They did not change a thing
outline.gist: The verb followed by its own root emphasises that they altered nothing in the agreement. The verse celebrates the men and women who stood their ground at the Trench and at Uhud.

outline.heading: Your covenant is not part-time
outline.gist: You need not be on a battlefield, where only a tiny share of the ummah dies. The covenant is all your life, spent working for the ummah's wellbeing until you die.

outline.heading: Shahid and siddiq: dying for Allah and living for Him
outline.gist: A shahid dies for the sake of Allah; a siddiq lives for Him for seventy, eighty or ninety years and stays on track, which is hard.

outline.heading: Abu Bakr, and those who will not leave their land
outline.gist: Abu Bakr was called al-Siddiq for accepting early and staying truthful to the end. People today who refuse to be pushed from their land, even as their homes are demolished, are true martyrs; our task is to be truthful for as long as we live.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: Scholarly views on when the last ten nights begin, and how quickly the month ends.

themes.label: Allah's laws in the world (sunan)
themes.note: Allah's laws make unity and justice the source of strength; Muslims must work within them rather than expect them broken.

themes.label: Time, opportunity and seizing the moment
themes.note: Use the strength of your middle years for Allah instead of waiting for old age.

themes.label: Youth, their challenges and their role
themes.note: Generations must cooperate: the young listen to elders, and elders train and empower the young as the Prophet did.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Like any relationship, the one with Allah grows dull unless nurtured.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: The Quran is enough and was the Prophet's only challenge; other wonders were signs of baraka.

themes.label: Tolerance, pluralism and dealing with difference
themes.note: Diversity of languages and races is a sign of Allah to celebrate; Islam keeps the good in cultures rather than Arabizing people.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Reviving dead earth shows Allah's power to raise the dead.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Listen to parents and grandparents: their wisdom comes from experience, not books.

themes.label: Knowing Allah / relationship with Allah
themes.note: Invest in your relationship with Allah until you long to rise at night to call on Him, as the Prophet did.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Believers sold their lives to Allah for Paradise; being true to that covenant is a lifelong, full-time commitment.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: Those who refuse to leave their land despite demolitions are true martyrs.

quran.point: Weakness, then strength, then weakness: a law telling us to use our strength now.
The surah opens with the Romans' defeat and later victory, which the Muslims celebrated.
He holds this verse is not about the reported splitting of the moon.
The verse recited at nearly every Muslim wedding, just before the verse on diversity.
The covenant: Allah has bought the believers' lives and wealth in return for Paradise.
Those who obey are with the prophets, the truthful, the martyrs and the righteous: the siddiq versus the shahid.

hadith.gist: Anas ibn Malik served in the Prophet's household as a boy of about ten and lived to teach for decades.
The splitting of the moon was witnessed and reported by very few companions.
Food increased when the Prophet placed his hand in it.
Allah descends to the lowest heaven in the last part of the night and asks who will call on Him, seek His forgiveness or ask of Him.
The Prophet asked Aisha's leave at night so he could rise and worship his Lord.

maxims: The ball is in our court
Islam is not here to Arabize people
Wisdom comes from experience, not books
Any relationship you don't invest in will die
A shahid dies for Allah; a siddiq lives for Him

stories.who: Anas ibn Malik, raised in the Prophet's house
stories.point: Youth who are empowered grow up to carry the legacy for generations.

stories.who: His teachers abroad objecting to his English khutbah
stories.point: Speaking to people in their language is right, while Arabic remains the key to the Quran.

stories.who: The Prophet rising from bed at night to pray
stories.point: A living relationship with Allah makes you long for night prayer.

stories.who: The defenders at the Trench and Uhud
stories.point: Truthfulness to the covenant with Allah, whether one dies early or lives long.

stories.who: Abu Bakr al-Siddiq
stories.point: Staying truthful to the covenant for a whole life earns the rank of siddiq.

contemporary: Palestinians refusing to leave their land as their homes are demolished
Elderly heads of state in their seventies and the struggle for power between generations
Outdoor Eid prayers where Muslims of many cultures wear their traditional dress
Scholars abroad objecting to khutbahs delivered in English
takeaways: Work within Allah's laws: build unity, justice, knowledge and wealth, and use your strength for Allah now rather than later.
Seek out the wisdom of parents, grandparents and elders; if you are older, train and empower the young.
Invest deliberately in your relationship with Allah, especially through night prayer, so worship does not grow dull.
Celebrate cultural diversity, keep what is good in your culture, and learn Arabic to understand the Quran directly.
Stay true to your covenant with Allah for your whole life, not part-time.

16:89.ar: وَيَوۡمَ نَبۡعَثُ فِي كُلِّ أُمَّةࣲ شَهِيدًا عَلَيۡهِم مِّنۡ أَنفُسِهِمۡۖ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ شَهِيدًا عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِۚ وَنَزَّلۡنَا عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ تِبۡيَٰنࣰ ا لِّكُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُدࣰ ى وَرَحۡمَةࣰ وَبُشۡرَىٰ لِلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
16:89.en: And (bethink you of) the day when We raise in every nation a witness against them of their own folk, and We bring thee (Muhammad) as a witness against these. And We reveal the Scripture unto thee as an exposition of all things, and a guidance and a mercy and good tidings for those who have surrendered (to Allah)

17:4.ar: وَقَضَيۡنَآ إِلَىٰ بَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ فِي ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ لَتُفۡسِدُنَّ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ مَرَّتَيۡنِ وَلَتَعۡلُنَّ عُلُوࣰّ ا كَبِيرࣰ ا
17:4.en: And We decreed for the Children of Israel in the Scripture: Ye verily will work corruption in the earth twice, and ye will become great tyrants

17:5.ar: فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ أُولَىٰهُمَا بَعَثۡنَا عَلَيۡكُمۡ عِبَادࣰ ا لَّنَآ أُوْلِي بَأۡسࣲ شَدِيدࣲ فَجَاسُواْ خِلَٰلَ ٱلدِّيَارِۚ وَكَانَ وَعۡدࣰ ا مَّفۡعُولࣰ ا
17:5.en: So when the time for the first of the two came, We roused against you slaves of Ours of great might who ravaged (your) country, and it was a threat performed

17:6.ar: ثُمَّ رَدَدۡنَا لَكُمُ ٱلۡكَرَّةَ عَلَيۡهِمۡ وَأَمۡدَدۡنَٰكُم بِأَمۡوَٰلࣲ وَبَنِينَ وَجَعَلۡنَٰكُمۡ أَكۡثَرَ نَفِيرًا
17:6.en: Then we gave you once again your turn against them, and We aided you with wealth and children and made you more in soldiery

17:7.ar: إِنۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ أَحۡسَنتُمۡ لِأَنفُسِكُمۡۖ وَإِنۡ أَسَأۡتُمۡ فَلَهَاۚ فَإِذَا جَآءَ وَعۡدُ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةِ لِيَسُـُٔواْ وُجُوهَكُمۡ وَلِيَدۡخُلُواْ ٱلۡمَسۡجِدَ كَمَا دَخَلُوهُ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةࣲ وَلِيُتَبِّرُواْ مَا عَلَوۡاْ تَتۡبِيرًا
17:7.en: (Saying): If ye do good, ye do good for your own souls, and if ye do evil, it is for them (in like manner). So, when the time for the second (of the judgments) came (We roused against you others of Our slaves) to ravage you, and to enter the Temple even as they entered it the first time, and to lay waste all that they conquered with an utter wasting

17:8.ar: عَسَىٰ رَبُّكُمۡ أَن يَرۡحَمَكُمۡۚ وَإِنۡ عُدتُّمۡ عُدۡنَاۚ وَجَعَلۡنَا جَهَنَّمَ لِلۡكَٰفِرِينَ حَصِيرًا
17:8.en: It may be that your Lord will have mercy on you, but if ye repeat (the crime) We shall repeat (the punishment), and We have appointed hell a dungeon for the disbelievers

17:53.ar: وَقُل لِّعِبَادِي يَقُولُواْ ٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ يَنزَغُ بَيۡنَهُمۡۚ إِنَّ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنَ كَانَ لِلۡإِنسَٰنِ عَدُوࣰّ ا مُّبِينࣰ ا
17:53.en: Tell My bondmen to speak that which is kindlier. Lo! the devil soweth discord among them. Lo! the devil is for man an open foe

17:70.ar: ۞وَلَقَدۡ كَرَّمۡنَا بَنِيٓ ءَادَمَ وَحَمَلۡنَٰهُمۡ فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِ وَرَزَقۡنَٰهُم مِّنَ ٱلطَّيِّبَٰتِ وَفَضَّلۡنَٰهُمۡ عَلَىٰ كَثِيرࣲ مِّمَّنۡ خَلَقۡنَا تَفۡضِيلࣰ ا
17:70.en: Verily we have honoured the Children of Adam. We carry them on the land and the sea, and have made provision of good things for them, and have preferred them above many of those whom We created with a marked preferment

18:9.ar: أَمۡ حَسِبۡتَ أَنَّ أَصۡحَٰبَ ٱلۡكَهۡفِ وَٱلرَّقِيمِ كَانُواْ مِنۡ ءَايَٰتِنَا عَجَبًا
18:9.en: Or deemest thou that the People of the Cave and the Inscription are a wonder among Our portents

4:41.ar: فَكَيۡفَ إِذَا جِئۡنَا مِن كُلِّ أُمَّةِۭ بِشَهِيدࣲ وَجِئۡنَا بِكَ عَلَىٰ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ شَهِيدࣰ ا
4:41.en: But how (will it be with them) when We bring of every people a witness, and We bring thee (O Muhammad) a witness against these
