ANpRZgkWb1c.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 14: Quranic Reflections on An-Nahl 80 to Al-Kahf 26
ANpRZgkWb1c.one_line: Closing the blessings cluster and opening the 'carrying the message' cluster: the Prophet as witness, prophecy and passivity, saying the best, human dignity, and the cave.
ANpRZgkWb1c.summary: He finishes the third cluster of surahs, about blessings and their source, and introduces the fourth, from Al-Isra onward, whose theme is that the Muslims now carry the message. Al-Isra hands them the baton, and Al-Kahf names four pillars a lasting nation needs: a clear idea, wealth, implementable knowledge and power. He ties the lack of these to the Muslim world's weakness and the impunity seen in Gaza, and asks each listener which pillar they serve. From An-Nahl 89 he argues that a witness from each nation proves the teaching is doable, which is why the Prophet is human, and that the Quran clarifies everything a person needs to do their job, gives guidance and mercy, and gives a believer something beautiful to look forward to. He reads Al-Isra 4-8 as past events in the history of the Children of Israel, not prophecies to wait on, and warns against waiting for a saviour. Al-Isra 53 commands saying what is best, which he defines as whatever most likely achieves the good outcome; otherwise, hold your tongue. Al-Isra 70 places human dignity beyond praise or criticism. Al-Kahf 9 shows a few young people starting a change they only saw centuries later.

outline.heading: Opening
Third cluster recap: blessings and their source
outline.gist: The surahs of the third cluster look at blessings from different angles: performing gratitude, recognising blessings as coming from Allah, and using them only by His law. Because they count Allah's gifts, they are beautiful choices for recitation in prayer.

outline.heading: Fourth cluster: carrying the message
outline.gist: From Al-Isra onward the surahs, mostly medium length, explain what carrying Islam to the world requires, the obstacles on the way and advice for those doing it. Having learned the story of faith and the meaning of blessings, the Muslim is now ready to carry it.

outline.heading: Al-Isra: the baton passes to this ummah
outline.gist: On the night journey the Prophet led the earlier prophets in prayer, symbolising that responsibility for the message now rests with him and his followers, and that it is carried through the Book of Allah.

outline.heading: Al-Kahf's first pillar of a nation: a clear idea
outline.gist: A civilisation that withstands time and fitnah needs four pillars. The first is a golden, clear message, as with the youth of the cave who knew exactly what they stood for.

outline.heading: Second pillar: wealth used properly
outline.gist: The story of the two men with the gardens teaches the proper use of wealth.

outline.heading: Third pillar: implementable knowledge
outline.gist: Musa thought he was the most knowledgeable and was shown what knowledge that can be applied looks like.

outline.heading: Fourth pillar: power and authority
outline.gist: Dhul-Qarnayn represents strength and authority used well.

outline.heading: Why we read Al-Kahf every week
outline.gist: Beyond its spiritual merit, the weekly reading reminds Muslims of what they lack. Without a nation they can still practise personally but cannot protect their own; the occupying state acts in Gaza without fear despite a billion people opposing it.

outline.heading: Which of the four pillars are you building?
outline.gist: Are you in politics and influence, academia, business, or raising awareness of the message and its values? Someone who contributes to none of the four is part of the problem.

outline.heading: Interlude
A witness from every nation proves it is doable
outline.gist: Shahid means a witness and an example: someone who lived the teaching so people can see it is practical. That is why the Prophet is human; nobody can emulate a demigod.

outline.heading: No slack for the persecuted Makkan Muslims
outline.gist: This was revealed to Muslims afraid to declare their faith, under real threat of death, yet they were told to emulate the Prophet and carry the message properly. The Makkan Quran did not excuse them because life was hard.

outline.heading: Clarification of everything you need
outline.gist: The Book clarifies everything a person needs to know who they are, why they are here and what their job is. It is a book of psychology, law, theology and sociology, not trigonometry or geography.

outline.heading: Guidance, compassion and good tidings
outline.gist: The Quran is guidance, an act of compassion from Allah, and good news for those who submit that things will be better, if not in this life then in the next.

outline.heading: Happiness as something good to look forward to
outline.gist: He likes an old philosopher's definition of happiness as having something enjoyable ahead. A Muslim living as he should always has Jannah ahead and is investing his time and wealth in building it.

outline.heading: Hospital staff living for a week off in June
outline.gist: Overworked health care workers endure months of misery for a trip to the Bahamas. If that makes them happy, eternity in Allah's presence should bring far more joy; if it does not, something is missing.

outline.heading: The two corruptions of Bani Israil are past history
outline.gist: These verses describe what the Torah foretold for the Children of Israel: two times they would cause corruption and lose the holy land. Both happened before the Prophet's time, so they are not prophecies about our era, though he still believes Palestinians' rights will be restored.

outline.heading: Prophecy as an excuse to wait for a saviour
outline.gist: People everywhere use prophecies to sit back and wait, like the 'chosen one' of film sagas. Waiting for a hero or a mahdi is the opposite of what the Prophet taught by word and deed.

outline.heading: A warning that it can happen again
outline.gist: The verses tell us what happened to them so we know it can happen to us. Returning the displaced to their land requires practical steps from each person; there is no concept in the deen of sitting and waiting.

outline.heading: Trust while working versus 'it will work out'
outline.gist: Saying it will work out is fine as tawakkul from someone working day and night. Said by spectators who observe and do nothing, it is a sick attitude.

outline.heading: Tell My servants to say what is best
outline.gist: Revealed around the tenth year, to companions still persecuted and unable to speak openly. They are told to say only what is best, from the root of ihsan, a rare expression in the Quran that raises the question of how 'best' is judged.

outline.heading: Defining 'the best': what most likely achieves the outcome
outline.gist: The best words are whatever is most likely to achieve the purpose of speaking. That forces the question of what the purpose is.

outline.heading: Turn the microscope inward: why am I saying this?
outline.gist: Before speaking, ask whether it is self-serving, to vent or settle a grudge, or because you want the other person to benefit and do well.

outline.heading: Nobody enjoys being told they were wrong
outline.gist: When advising, pointing out someone's mistake feels sweet only to the one doing it. He acts out a person savouring an 'I told you so' for twenty-five years, down to the latte at the Tim Hortons, as an example of the self-serving kind of speech.

outline.heading: The best keeps the door back to Allah open
outline.gist: The aim is that people learn, improve and draw closer to Allah, which can take serious reflection before speaking. Being right is not enough: some ways of saying the truth bring people back, others slam the door forever.

outline.heading: Shaytan exploits words that are good but not the best
outline.gist: The verse warns that Shaytan sows discord. He uses any imperfect phrasing to suggest a condescending tone or hidden meaning and break relationships. If you cannot say the best, hold your tongue.

outline.heading: Allah dignified the children of Adam
outline.gist: A cardinal verse: every human being is dignified by Allah simply for being human. In an era of depression, low self-esteem and inferiority, one cause is not grasping that this value is granted by God and no one can touch it.

outline.heading: Mistreatment cannot remove your value
outline.gist: Humiliation, mistreatment or prison do not touch the value Allah decreed. We are commanded to honour one another, and those who are not honoured must know their worth was never in others' hands.

outline.heading: Good deeds do not raise your value
outline.gist: Your value is fixed. You do good to reach your potential, experience Allah's love and be close to Him, and avoid sin so as not to be ungrateful or miss the opportunity, not to raise or lower your worth.

outline.heading: Criticism and praise as feedback, not worth
outline.gist: Take from harsh criticism what helps you improve, and take praise as a sign the work was good. Children need careful praise because they cannot yet separate the two; adults should know their value is sacred.

outline.heading: The cave and the tablet of their principles
outline.gist: Al-Raqim was the tablet where the youth wrote down what they stood for, their mission and vision, a detail people forget when they speak only of the people of the cave.

outline.heading: A few youths changed a corrupt kingdom
outline.gist: A handful of teenagers and a dog did social and religious work in a rotten kingdom. Allah bent the laws of nature, put them to sleep for three hundred years, and they woke to a kingdom transformed by what they began.

outline.heading: Why they woke for half a day and then died
outline.gist: They woke only so Allah could show them their impact: look at what you sparked, even if it took three centuries.

outline.heading: Not a one-time sign
outline.gist: The verse asks whether we thought this was a one-off wonder. Allah can do it again for anyone who dedicates their life to a cause and trusts their impact even if they never see it.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Lays out how the surahs fall into thematic clusters, from blessings to carrying the message, and why knowing the theme helps one connect to recitation in prayer.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The Muslims have been handed the baton of the prophets and must carry the message to the world through the Book of Allah.

themes.label: Activism, civic engagement and the path forward
themes.note: Al-Kahf's four pillars of a lasting nation: a clear message, wealth, applicable knowledge and power. Everyone should be strengthening one of them.

themes.label: Palestine, Gaza and the suffering of Muslims
themes.note: The occupying state acts without fear in Gaza because the Muslims lack the pillars of a strong nation.

themes.label: The Prophet's attributes, character and example
themes.note: The Prophet is the human witness who proves the teaching can be lived, and the persecuted companions were expected to emulate him.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: A believer always has Jannah to look forward to, which should bring more joy than any holiday.

themes.label: Agency, responsibility and rejecting victim mentality
themes.note: Using prophecies to wait for a saviour is anti-prophetic; the return of the displaced requires each person's practical work.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Trusting that Allah will work things out is right only for someone doing their absolute best.

themes.label: Guarding the tongue; speech and gossip
themes.note: Say what is best, meaning whatever most likely helps the listener; check your motive first, keep the door to Allah open, and otherwise stay silent.

themes.label: Shaytan: his methods and how to resist him
themes.note: Shaytan seizes on imperfect phrasing to plant suspicion and destroy relationships.

themes.label: Self-value, self-worth, confidence
themes.note: Human dignity is granted by Allah and fixed: mistreatment, deeds, criticism and praise neither raise nor lower it.

themes.label: Quranic stories and their lessons
themes.note: The youth of the cave wrote down their principles, did their part, and woke to see their impact centuries later.

quran.point: The scene of a witness from every nation, with the Prophet as witness, recurs after the Hijrah.

hadith.gist: On the night journey the Prophet led the earlier prophets in prayer in Jerusalem.

maxims: If you can't say the best, hold your tongue

Your value doesn't go up and doesn't go down

stories.point: If a week away makes people bear months of misery, the promise of Jannah should fill a believer with joy.

contemporary: The war on Gaza over the preceding six months and the occupying state's impunity
Stress and burnout among physicians, nurses and other health care workers
Saviour narratives in film sagas such as Star Wars and The Matrix
Widespread depression, low self-esteem and inferiority complexes today
takeaways: Choose one of the four pillars (message, wealth, applicable knowledge, power) and work to strengthen it.
Do not use prophecies as a reason to wait; take practical steps and trust Allah while working.
Before speaking or advising, ask what you want to achieve and choose the words most likely to help; otherwise stay silent.
Anchor your self-worth in the dignity Allah gave you; treat criticism and praise as feedback only.
Do your part even if the impact will not be visible in your lifetime.

13:19.ar: ۞أَفَمَن يَعۡلَمُ أَنَّمَآ أُنزِلَ إِلَيۡكَ مِن رَّبِّكَ ٱلۡحَقُّ كَمَنۡ هُوَ أَعۡمَىٰٓۚ إِنَّمَا يَتَذَكَّرُ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
13:19.en: Is he who knoweth that what is revealed unto thee from thy Lord is the truth like him who is blind? But only men of understanding heed

13:20.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يُوفُونَ بِعَهۡدِ ٱللَّهِ وَلَا يَنقُضُونَ ٱلۡمِيثَٰقَ
13:20.en: Such as keep the pact of Allah, and break not the covenant

13:21.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَصِلُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيَخۡشَوۡنَ رَبَّهُمۡ وَيَخَافُونَ سُوٓءَ ٱلۡحِسَابِ
13:21.en: Such as unite that which Allah hath commandeth should be joined, and fear their Lord, and dread a woeful reckoning

13:22.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ صَبَرُواْ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ وَجۡهِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَأَقَامُواْ ٱلصَّلَوٰةَ وَأَنفَقُواْ مِمَّا رَزَقۡنَٰهُمۡ سِرࣰّ ا وَعَلَانِيَةࣰ وَيَدۡرَءُونَ بِٱلۡحَسَنَةِ ٱلسَّيِّئَةَ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
13:22.en: Such as persevere in seeking their Lord's Countenance and are regular in prayer and spend of that which We bestow upon them secretly and openly, and overcome evil with good. Theirs will be the sequel of the (heavenly) Home

13:23.ar: جَنَّٰتُ عَدۡنࣲ يَدۡخُلُونَهَا وَمَن صَلَحَ مِنۡ ءَابَآئِهِمۡ وَأَزۡوَٰجِهِمۡ وَذُرِّيَّٰتِهِمۡۖ وَٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةُ يَدۡخُلُونَ عَلَيۡهِم مِّن كُلِّ بَابࣲ‏
13:23.en: Gardens of Eden which they enter, along with all who do right of their fathers and their helpmeets and their seed. The angels enter unto them from every gate

13:24.ar: سَلَٰمٌ عَلَيۡكُم بِمَا صَبَرۡتُمۡۚ فَنِعۡمَ عُقۡبَى ٱلدَّارِ
13:24.en: (Saying): Peace be unto you because ye persevered. Ah, passing sweet will be the sequel of the (heavenly) Home

13:25.ar: وَٱلَّذِينَ يَنقُضُونَ عَهۡدَ ٱللَّهِ مِنۢ بَعۡدِ مِيثَٰقِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعُونَ مَآ أَمَرَ ٱللَّهُ بِهِۦٓ أَن يُوصَلَ وَيُفۡسِدُونَ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمُ ٱللَّعۡنَةُ وَلَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ ٱلدَّارِ
13:25.en: And those who break the covenant of Allah after ratifying it, and sever that which Allah hath commanded should be joined, and make mischief in the earth: theirs is the curse and theirs the ill abode

22:46.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ يَعۡقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ ءَاذَانࣱ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
22:46.en: Have they not travelled in the land, and have they hearts wherewith to feel and ears wherewith to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts, which are within the bosoms, that grow blind

41:34.ar: وَلَا تَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡحَسَنَةُ وَلَا ٱلسَّيِّئَةُۚ ٱدۡفَعۡ بِٱلَّتِي هِيَ أَحۡسَنُ فَإِذَا ٱلَّذِي بَيۡنَكَ وَبَيۡنَهُۥ عَدَٰوَةࣱ كَأَنَّهُۥ وَلِيٌّ حَمِيمࣱ‏
41:34.en: The good deed and the evil deed are not alike. Repel the evil deed with one which is better, then lo! he, between whom and thee there was enmity (will become) as though he was a bosom friend

QacXqmF0J3o.speaker: adnan
QacXqmF0J3o.speaker_note: continues his own weekend Al-Ra'd series and describes the covenant taken from him when he received his Quran certification
QacXqmF0J3o.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 5
QacXqmF0J3o.one_line: Explains 13:19-25: belief in the Quran as truth must be proven by a bundle of traits, from keeping covenants to repelling evil with good.
QacXqmF0J3o.summary: He calls 13:19-25 the ethics of haqq. Blindness in the Quran is of the heart: seeing without learning, like seeing a road sign and still driving off the cliff. Two people who believe different things cannot behave the same, so belief needs proof, and on Judgment Day your book is that proof. The traits follow. Keeping Allah's covenant: he explains covenant and pledge through the chain-of-transmission tradition he was raised in, the companions' pledges to the Prophet, the youth the Prophet refused until he repented, and a former enemy told that Islam erases what came before. Joining every tie Allah ordered joined, from parents to the ummah. Reverence, which mixes fear, exaltation and love, and fear of a hard reckoning. Patience for Allah's sake, prayer, spending secretly and openly, and repelling evil with good. Responding in kind makes you a mirror with no essence; like Isa and the Prophet, never hand anyone the remote control of your reactions. The traits are bundled, not ranked, mixing ritual and ethics, and he criticizes reducing Islam to rituals. Their reward is the Gardens of Eden, joined by righteous relatives, so strengthen ties because you never know whom Allah loves. Covenant-breakers, tie-cutters and spreaders of corruption get the worst abode.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: the law of haqq, and today the ethics of haqq
outline.gist: After the law of haqq and the law of change, these verses describe the behaviour Allah expects from people of truth.

outline.heading: One who knows the truth versus one who is blind
outline.gist: In the Quran blindness almost always means blindness of the heart, not of the eyes.

outline.heading: Seeing without learning is blindness
outline.gist: Seeing the sign that the road ends and not turning is no different from never seeing it.

outline.heading: People of essence: those who reflect
outline.gist: Lubb is the core of a thing; only those who use their reason benefit from what follows.

outline.heading: Different beliefs must produce different behaviour
outline.gist: If a believer and a denier behave the same, one of them has not really done what they claim.

outline.heading: A claim of faith needs proof
outline.gist: Inner belief without visible evidence carries no weight; your book on Judgment Day is where the claim is tested.

outline.heading: Fulfilling Allah's covenant and not breaking the pledge
outline.gist: A covenant is asked and a pledge given; he received his own when certified in Quran memorization.

outline.heading: Covenant and pledge in the chain of transmission
outline.gist: Every discipline was handed down with a binding pledge to keep teaching it, which preserved the authenticity of the knowledge.

outline.heading: The companions' pledges to the Prophet
outline.gist: Outside politics, bay'ah was a personal contract: the pillars, sincerity to every Muslim, and taking from the world only a traveller's provision.

outline.heading: Contracts sealed by a handshake
outline.gist: Marriage was once sealed by witnesses and a handshake; the sheikh is the least necessary person at a nikah.

outline.heading: The youth whose pledge the Prophet refused
outline.gist: A young man who had tugged a woman's garment the night before was turned away until he promised never to repeat it.

outline.heading: Islam erases what came before it
outline.gist: A former leading enemy made his pledge conditional on forgiveness and was told that Islam wipes out the past.

outline.heading: You too made a covenant and will read your book
outline.gist: Every Muslim has pledged; on reading their book, those who did not live by it will search the pages for any proof.

outline.heading: Joining what Allah ordered to be joined
outline.gist: The wording is general: parents, siblings, children, spouse, extended family, neighbours and the ummah.

outline.heading: Reverence of their Lord and fear of a hard reckoning
outline.gist: Khashyah mixes fear of just punishment, exaltation of Allah and love; they fear being judged badly.

outline.heading: Ethics and spirituality are never separated
outline.gist: Quranic lists always mix moral and spiritual traits; reducing Islam to rituals means misunderstanding the deen.

outline.heading: Patience seeking the face of their Lord
outline.gist: Patience alone is not enough; it must be for the right reason, to please Allah.

outline.heading: Prayer and spending secretly and openly
outline.gist: They establish prayer and spend from what Allah gave them, in private and in public.

outline.heading: Repelling evil with good
outline.gist: They protect themselves from evil by actively doing good in return.

outline.heading: The traits are a bundle, not a ranking
outline.gist: Allah could easily have grouped rituals first and ethics after; He bundled them so none can be dropped.

outline.heading: Why returning good for evil is so hard
outline.gist: The ego feels it rewards bad behaviour; it takes months of training for people to accept it.

outline.heading: Don't be a mirror
outline.gist: If you only reflect how others treat you, you have no essence and represent nothing.

outline.heading: Isa: everyone gives what is inside them
outline.gist: Insulted from afar, Isa replied with kindness, explaining that each person produces what they carry inside.

outline.heading: Never hand anyone the remote control
outline.gist: The Prophet was described as growing more patient the ruder people were; your responses must stay yours.

outline.heading: Theirs is the final abode
outline.gist: Those with these traits will have the good ending, explained in the next verse.

outline.heading: Gardens of Eden with the righteous of their families
outline.gist: Parents, spouses and children with some righteousness follow them in, a blessing of having pious people in your family.

outline.heading: Strengthen ties: you never know whom Allah loves
outline.gist: It is often the relative you least expect; neglecting ties may cost you being counted among those who follow them.

outline.heading: Angels at every gate: peace for your patience
outline.gist: Angels greet and serve them, saying peace be upon you for your patience; excellent is the final home.

outline.heading: Drop one trait and no one can say you qualify
outline.gist: He lists the seven or eight traits; since Allah set no order or conditions, no scholar can say what happens if one is missing.

outline.heading: Those who break the covenant and sever ties
outline.gist: The same general wording describes the opposite: breaking the pledge and cutting what Allah ordered joined.

outline.heading: Corruption spreads from the inside out
outline.gist: Corruption sums up the opposite of the other traits; inner corruption eventually affects everything around it, earning the worst abode.

outline.heading: Haqq has people who stand for it; Islam is simple

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt

themes.label: Values, principles and ethics as a system
themes.note: The verses bundle ritual and moral traits as one system; compartmentalizing them or reducing Islam to rituals is a misunderstanding.

themes.label: Oaths, promises, trust and loyalty
themes.note: Every Muslim has made a covenant with Allah; he explains covenant and pledge through scholarly transmission and the companions' pledges.

themes.label: Seeking knowledge, learning and scholars
themes.note: Knowledge was preserved through oral transmission and binding pledges to keep teaching.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Joining what Allah ordered covers every relationship from parents outward to the ummah.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Reverence mixes fear, exaltation and love; fear of a bad reckoning makes people ask before they act.

themes.label: Intention and sincerity (niyyah, ikhlas)
themes.note: Patience counts only when it is for the sake of Allah.

themes.label: Character and manners (akhlaq)
themes.note: Repelling evil with good keeps your conduct your own instead of mirroring others.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Gardens of Eden shared with righteous family and greeted by angels, against the worst abode for covenant-breakers.

25:63.ar: وَعِبَادُ ٱلرَّحۡمَٰنِ ٱلَّذِينَ يَمۡشُونَ عَلَى ٱلۡأَرۡضِ هَوۡنࣰ ا وَإِذَا خَاطَبَهُمُ ٱلۡجَٰهِلُونَ قَالُواْ سَلَٰمࣰ ا

27:21.en: I verily will punish him with hard punishment or I verily will slay him, or he verily shall bring me a plain excuse

27:22.ar: فَمَكَثَ غَيۡرَ بَعِيدࣲ فَقَالَ أَحَطتُ بِمَا لَمۡ تُحِطۡ بِهِۦ وَجِئۡتُكَ مِن سَبَإِۭ بِنَبَإࣲ يَقِينٍ
27:22.en: But he was not long in coming, and he said: I have found out (a thing) that thou apprehendest not, and I come unto thee from Sheba with sure tidings

27:23.ar: إِنِّي وَجَدتُّ ٱمۡرَأَةࣰ تَمۡلِكُهُمۡ وَأُوتِيَتۡ مِن كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَلَهَا عَرۡشٌ عَظِيمࣱ‏
27:23.en: Lo! I found a woman ruling over them, and she hath been given (abundance) of all things, and hers is a mighty throne

27:24.ar: وَجَدتُّهَا وَقَوۡمَهَا يَسۡجُدُونَ لِلشَّمۡسِ مِن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَزَيَّنَ لَهُمُ ٱلشَّيۡطَٰنُ أَعۡمَٰلَهُمۡ فَصَدَّهُمۡ عَنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ فَهُمۡ لَا يَهۡتَدُونَ

27:26.en: Allah; there is no Allah save Him, the Lord of the Tremendous Throne

2:258.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ إِلَى ٱلَّذِي حَآجَّ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ فِي رَبِّهِۦٓ أَنۡ ءَاتَىٰهُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُلۡكَ إِذۡ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ رَبِّيَ ٱلَّذِي يُحۡيِۦ وَيُمِيتُ قَالَ أَنَا۠ أُحۡيِۦ وَأُمِيتُۖ قَالَ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمُ فَإِنَّ ٱللَّهَ يَأۡتِي بِٱلشَّمۡسِ مِنَ ٱلۡمَشۡرِقِ فَأۡتِ بِهَا مِنَ ٱلۡمَغۡرِبِ فَبُهِتَ ٱلَّذِي كَفَرَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:258.en: Bethink thee of him who had an argument with Abraham about his Lord, because Allah had given him the kingdom; how, when Abraham said: My Lord is He Who giveth life and causeth death, he answered: I give life and cause death. Abraham said: Lo! Allah causeth the sun to rise in the East, so do thou cause it to come up from the West. Thus was the disbeliever abashed. And Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

2:124.ar: ۞وَإِذِ ٱبۡتَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِـۧمَ رَبُّهُۥ بِكَلِمَٰتࣲ فَأَتَمَّهُنَّۖ قَالَ إِنِّي جَاعِلُكَ لِلنَّاسِ إِمَامࣰ اۖ قَالَ وَمِن ذُرِّيَّتِيۖ قَالَ لَا يَنَالُ عَهۡدِي ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
2:124.en: And (remember) when his Lord tried Abraham with (His) commands, and he fulfilled them, He said: Lo! I have appointed thee a leader for mankind. (Abraham) said: And of my offspring (will there be leaders)? He said: My covenant includeth not wrong-doers

vjiTIwtOdcU.speaker: adnan
vjiTIwtOdcU.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; speaks as a hospital physician and mentions the Imam Development Academy at MWN
vjiTIwtOdcU.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 18: Quranic Reflections on Al-Furqan 1 to An-Naml 44
vjiTIwtOdcU.one_line: Wrapping up the cluster on carrying the message: abandoning the Quran, the servants of the Most Merciful, exemplars, 'He cures me', and the hoopoe's passion.
vjiTIwtOdcU.summary: He sums up the fourth cluster: Al-Furqan names obstacles in carrying the message and ends with the traits that overcome them, Ash-Shuara shows how propaganda and public narrative shape reception of the message, and An-Naml shows that the strong never follow the weak, so Muslims need collective strength. He then retraces the whole cluster from Al-Isra. On Al-Furqan 30 he warns that many Muslims, practising ones included, have turned their backs on the Quran, displaying it without understanding it, and urges using Ramadan to listen and learn. The servants of the Most Merciful walk humbly and answer the ignorant with peace, as Ibrahim moved on from the king's foolish argument. Al-Furqan 74 is a prayer for spouses and children close to Allah and to become an exemplar, the Quranic meaning of imam. From Ibrahim's 'when I am ill, He cures me' he explains that doctors treat while Allah cures, and urges Muslim families to accept when medicine has nothing left to offer at the end of life. Sulayman's roll call shows that movements without discipline go nowhere, and the hoopoe's distress at a people not worshipping Allah is the passion he wants to see.

outline.heading: Opening
Recap: the individual and the community
outline.gist: Al-Muminun stressed investing in the individual and An-Nur the community that must carry and protect the message.

outline.heading: Al-Furqan: obstacles and the ethics to overcome them
outline.gist: The surah lists the major challenges that arise every time the message is carried and closes with the traits of the servants of the Most Merciful. Its final verses are a safe, beautiful choice for leading prayer in an unfamiliar masjid.

outline.heading: Ash-Shuara: the effect of public narrative
outline.gist: He has written several papers comparing this surah with others. It looks at the message from the angle of the public eye and propaganda.

outline.heading: Poets as the media of their age
outline.gist: Musa's story here is told as public opinion saw it: a bunch of hooligans. The surah is named after the poets because their verses carried the news people accepted as fact, whether or not it happened.

outline.heading: Quraysh's paid poets and the poetry of the seerah
outline.gist: Quraysh paid poets to insult the Prophet and retell events. Early seerah sources are mostly poetry, which readers skip, but it shows the battle of narratives.

outline.heading: Today's propagandists and our weak narrative
outline.gist: Commentators spout incoherent, false claims to millions while intelligent people accept them. Muslims lack the ability to shape the public narrative.

outline.heading: An-Naml: the strong never follow the weak
outline.gist: The weak imitate the strong in dress, speech and manner, as was observed centuries ago. For the message to be heard Muslims need collective strength, stability and unity.

outline.heading: Isolated prophets versus Sulayman's kingdom
outline.gist: Salih and Lut were isolated and went unheard, while Sulayman's strength brought a whole kingdom to the faith. Power affects the message and the message affects power.

outline.heading: Recap of the cluster: Al-Isra to Al-Anbiya
outline.gist: You carry the baton through the Quran; you need a clear idea, wealth, applicable knowledge and power; the family is the unit; the message brings fulfilment even under persecution; the prophets are your role models.

outline.heading: Recap of the cluster: Al-Hajj to An-Naml
outline.gist: It is a journey needing grit and flexibility; invest in individuals, then the community, which must be enlightened to carry it; watch for the obstacles, guard against hostile narratives and build your own; and without strength and unity no one will listen.

outline.heading: Our main function in the West
outline.gist: Carrying the message for ourselves and to those who lack it is the main role of Muslims in the West, so these surahs must be studied to know what doing it right requires.

outline.heading: A verse for each of us in the month of the Quran
outline.gist: The verse names one of the obstacles the surah lists, and it is addressed to everyone, especially in Ramadan.

outline.heading: The Messenger's complaint and what 'Quran' means
outline.gist: The messenger may be Muhammad or every prophet; he prefers the second. 'Quran' means something recited, with rules for its recitation, and meant for contemplation, not only letters.

outline.heading: Mahjur: turning your back on it
outline.gist: Hajr is deliberately avoiding something, as in the hadith forbidding a Muslim to shun his brother beyond three days, where the better one initiates the greeting. People stop reciting the Quran, stop learning from it and forget what it means.

outline.heading: A Quran hung in the car
outline.gist: It becomes an object for baraka: hung in the car, opened in gold in the living room, framed on the wall.

outline.heading: Following a book you never read
outline.gist: People show off copies from Hajj without knowing what is in them. He quotes the saying that the most dangerous person follows one book they never read; Ramadan is for reconnecting.

outline.heading: Why the whole Quran is recited in prayer
outline.gist: A quick prayer with short recitation would make him popular, but you must listen to the book you believe in. Stand, listen, and go home to look up what confused you.

outline.heading: Even practising Muslims are disconnected
outline.gist: The companions had questions and admitted when they did not know, referring others to Ibn Abbas. Today many practising Muslims neither read, understand nor contemplate the Quran, and others kiss it but follow nothing in it.

outline.heading: The solution: the servants of the Most Merciful
outline.gist: After listing challenges, the surah offers its solution through these people's traits, and the description itself is the first trait.

outline.heading: Servants, not defenders, of the Most Compassionate
outline.gist: Allah needs no one to defend Him; He wants servants who serve His message and His people and defend justice. If He is the Most Compassionate, His servants are the most compassionate.

outline.heading: Walking on earth with humility
outline.gist: Hawn is ease and humbleness, not a rule about stomping. They do not walk with arrogance, intimidation or a sense of superiority.

outline.heading: Saying peace to the ignorant: Ibrahim and the king
outline.gist: When the tyrant king answered 'my Lord gives life and death' by killing one man and freeing another, Ibrahim did not argue the absurdity; he moved to the sun rising from the east.

outline.heading: Peace cannot coexist with arrogance
outline.gist: It is not about being right or silencing the other person. Salam excludes arrogance, so show love and ease and do not burn bridges; some people need time to find their way.

outline.heading: Thanking a critic who misunderstood
outline.gist: People often criticise him over a point they misunderstood or half heard. Rather than re-argue the whole talk, he thanks them for the feedback, a restraint that took him years to learn.

outline.heading: A verse behind the Imam Development Academy
outline.gist: This verse is dear to him and part of how he explains the mission and vision of the Muslim Wellness Network.

outline.heading: Spouses and children who are the coolness of the eye
outline.gist: The phrase means inner happiness and peace. Ask for a spouse and children who bring you joy because they live as Allah wants and bring you closer to Him.

outline.heading: Not wealth, but closeness to Allah
outline.gist: Their success or riches mean nothing if they do not know God. Then you ask to be made a leader of the pious: not to be given an imam, but to become one.

outline.heading: What 'imam' really means
outline.gist: In the West it means whoever leads prayer; in the Middle East it is reserved for the great scholars. In the Quran it means an exemplar, as Allah told Ibrahim He would make him an imam.

outline.heading: Ibrahim: an exemplar with few followers
outline.gist: Ibrahim had very few followers in his life and is now the figure most of humanity agrees on, because he lived by example. The academy aims to develop such people, who understand the principles and live them.

outline.heading: Make me one who leads by living it
outline.gist: The prayer asks to live Islam to its highest standard and lead the way by example.

outline.heading: Ibrahim speaks beautifully of his Lord
outline.gist: Amid a surah about public narrative, Ibrahim describes Allah to his people with remarkable beauty, more so here than in other surahs.

outline.heading: I treat; Allah cures
outline.gist: When I am ill, He cures me. As a physician he has never cured anyone; he treats with the tools he has, and the cure comes from Allah.

outline.heading: Code status discussions with Muslim families
outline.gist: Almost weekly he speaks with Muslim families of very old, very sick relatives with advanced cancer or dementia, when doctors have nothing left to offer.

outline.heading: Declining treatment is not killing
outline.gist: Families feel stopping fluids and antibiotics means killing a loved one, but refusing medication is a Muslim's right; killing yourself means taking something harmful. The Quran gives principles, while medicine decides what treats what.

outline.heading: 'Nothing else to offer' dooms no one
outline.gist: A shelf of medicines does not mean one of them fits the disease. When the team has nothing to offer they are not condemning the patient, because they never offered a cure in the first place.

outline.heading: CPR on bones riddled with cancer
outline.gist: Expertise may say CPR or intubation will not help and would only break ribs. Doing nothing is allowed; if Allah wills a cure, it will come.

outline.heading: Medicine was not designed to prevent death
outline.gist: We use evidence-based treatment to show Allah we did our best, and when no reasonable measure remains we let things be, with peace and acceptance.

outline.heading: Called in on his day off
outline.gist: Muslim communities are very poor at this. He was pulled from a haircut with his son for a two-and-a-half-hour discussion with a family who would not let a very ill relative go.

outline.heading: Turn to Allah for the cure
outline.gist: Doctors offer what they can and then stop; if you thought the medicine was the cure all along, that is the problem.

outline.heading: Sulayman's roll call: the hoopoe is missing
outline.gist: Sulayman ran a strict army of humans and creatures, with a morning routine and attendance. The hoopoe was absent.

outline.heading: Movements without discipline go nowhere
outline.gist: Sulayman would punish the hoopoe unless it brought a clear excuse. Every successful movement in history ran this way, and an ummah that wants to get something done needs discipline.

outline.heading: No commitment in masjid work
outline.gist: In his years of masjid work people show up late or only when nothing else ranks higher. Nothing in dawah or community building works without commitment.

outline.heading: 'Busy' means it didn't make your list
outline.gist: His patience is wearing thin. You always have time; be honest and say it did not make the cut instead of claiming to be busy.

outline.heading: The hoopoe's excuse: a people not worshipping Allah
outline.gist: On its errand the hoopoe found a wealthy, powerful people who did not know Allah. It was so disturbed it gathered information and tried to call them, and came back late.

outline.heading: News you do not have: the queen of Sheba
outline.gist: It told the prophet-king of a queen with a great throne whose people prostrated to the sun instead of Allah.

outline.heading: We need a hundred thousand hoopoes
outline.gist: Why do they not worship the One who brings out what is hidden in the heavens and earth and knows what we conceal? He wants that passion multiplied.

outline.heading: Passion that was ordinary in Sulayman's army
outline.gist: Sulayman was not impressed because his whole army loved Allah that way. We need people who are pained to see someone far from Allah and who go out to teach them.

themes.label: Media and controlling the narrative
themes.note: Ash-Shuara shows propaganda shaping how the message is received; Muslims today lack a public narrative to counter false commentators.

themes.label: Unity of the ummah
themes.note: The strong never follow the weak, so the message needs collective strength, stability and unity.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: A full recap of the cluster on carrying the message, the main function of Muslims in the West.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Abandoning the Quran means treating it as an ornament without reading, understanding or following it; Ramadan is for reconnecting.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: The servants of the Most Merciful walk humbly and answer the ignorant with peace rather than arguments to win.

themes.label: Family: parents, relatives, kinship ties
themes.note: Pray for spouses and children whose closeness to Allah brings you inner joy, rather than worldly success.

themes.label: Leadership, governance and institutions
themes.note: An imam in the Quranic sense is an exemplar who leads by living Islam, which is what the Imam Development Academy aims to produce.

themes.label: Visiting the sick, caring for elders and the vulnerable
themes.note: Muslim families must learn to accept when medicine has nothing left to offer a dying relative; declining futile treatment is not killing.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Doctors treat and Allah cures; treatment is taking the means, and the outcome rests with Him.

themes.label: Discipline and commitment in collective work
themes.note: Sulayman's roll call shows movements need discipline; masjid work suffers from people who show up only when convenient.

themes.label: Dawah, outreach and representing Islam
themes.note: The hoopoe's distress at people not worshipping Allah is the passion the ummah needs to teach those far from Him.

Companions admitted when they did not know a word's meaning and referred people to Ibn Abbas.

I treat; Allah cures
Salam and arrogance are mutually exclusive

stories.point: The enemies of the message fought it through the media of their day, the public narrative.

stories.who: His habit of thanking critics who misunderstood him
stories.point: Letting go out of respect and mercy takes years to learn but is the first trait of Allah's servants.

stories.who: Ibrahim as an exemplar with few followers
stories.point: Living by example made him the most followed person on earth.

contemporary: Media commentators reaching millions with false claims while Muslims lack a public narrative

takeaways: Reconnect with the Quran this Ramadan: listen in prayer, look up what confused you and act on it.
Answer ignorant or hostile people with peace; do not argue to win or burn bridges.
Ask Allah for a family close to Him and to make you an exemplar who lives Islam.
Remember that doctors treat and Allah cures, and accept when medicine has nothing more to offer a dying relative.
Bring discipline and honest commitment to community work, and care enough about people far from Allah to go and teach them.

8:41.ar: ۞وَٱعۡلَمُوٓاْ أَنَّمَا غَنِمۡتُم مِّن شَيۡءࣲ فَأَنَّ لِلَّهِ خُمُسَهُۥ وَلِلرَّسُولِ وَلِذِي ٱلۡقُرۡبَىٰ وَٱلۡيَتَٰمَىٰ وَٱلۡمَسَٰكِينِ وَٱبۡنِ ٱلسَّبِيلِ إِن كُنتُمۡ ءَامَنتُم بِٱللَّهِ وَمَآ أَنزَلۡنَا عَلَىٰ عَبۡدِنَا يَوۡمَ ٱلۡفُرۡقَانِ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡتَقَى ٱلۡجَمۡعَانِۗ وَٱللَّهُ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرٌ
8:41.en: And know that whatever ye take as spoils of war, lo! a fifth thereof is for Allah, and for the messenger and for the kinsman (who hath need) and orphans and the needy and the wayfarer, if ye believe in Allah and that which We revealed unto Our slave on the Day of Discrimination, the day when the two armies met. And Allah is Able to do all things

8:5.ar: كَمَآ أَخۡرَجَكَ رَبُّكَ مِنۢ بَيۡتِكَ بِٱلۡحَقِّ وَإِنَّ فَرِيقࣰ ا مِّنَ ٱلۡمُؤۡمِنِينَ لَكَٰرِهُونَ
8:5.en: Even as thy Lord caused thee (Muhammad) to go forth from thy home with the Truth, and lo! a party of the believers were averse (to it)

8:6.ar: يُجَٰدِلُونَكَ فِي ٱلۡحَقِّ بَعۡدَ مَا تَبَيَّنَ كَأَنَّمَا يُسَاقُونَ إِلَى ٱلۡمَوۡتِ وَهُمۡ يَنظُرُونَ
8:6.en: Disputing with thee of the Truth after it had been made manifest, as if they were being driven to death visible

8:7.ar: وَإِذۡ يَعِدُكُمُ ٱللَّهُ إِحۡدَى ٱلطَّآئِفَتَيۡنِ أَنَّهَا لَكُمۡ وَتَوَدُّونَ أَنَّ غَيۡرَ ذَاتِ ٱلشَّوۡكَةِ تَكُونُ لَكُمۡ وَيُرِيدُ ٱللَّهُ أَن يُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ بِكَلِمَٰتِهِۦ وَيَقۡطَعَ دَابِرَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
8:7.en: And when Allah promised you one of the two bands (of the enemy) that it should be yours, and ye longed that other than the armed one might be yours. And Allah willed that He should cause the Truth to triumph by His words, and cut the root of the disbelievers

8:8.ar: لِيُحِقَّ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَيُبۡطِلَ ٱلۡبَٰطِلَ وَلَوۡ كَرِهَ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُونَ
8:8.en: That He might cause the Truth to triumph and bring vanity to naught, however much the guilty might oppose

8:1.ar: يَسۡـَٔلُونَكَ عَنِ ٱلۡأَنفَالِۖ قُلِ ٱلۡأَنفَالُ لِلَّهِ وَٱلرَّسُولِۖ فَٱتَّقُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَأَصۡلِحُواْ ذَاتَ بَيۡنِكُمۡۖ وَأَطِيعُواْ ٱللَّهَ وَرَسُولَهُۥٓ إِن كُنتُم مُّؤۡمِنِينَ
8:1.en: They ask thee (O Muhammad) of the spoils of war. Say: The spoils of war belong to Allah and the messenger, so keep your duty to Allah, and adjust the matter of your difference, and obey Allah and His messenger, if ye are (true) believers

CODVakTQ4iw.speaker: adnan
CODVakTQ4iw.speaker_note: speaks of being exiled from Syria, his seerah classes, and his city-wide attendance count of 6,500
CODVakTQ4iw.title: An Additional Three Ramadan Reminders
CODVakTQ4iw.one_line: On the 19th of Ramadan: Badr teaches that reclaiming rights is not about wealth, recommit to the last ten nights, and fasting lets the soul be heard.
CODVakTQ4iw.summary: Two days after the anniversary of Badr, he first reflects on six months of what he calls the first genocide documented live. The early demand that Muslims condemn the resistance, he argues, was a tactic to narrow the range of acceptable opinion. Having watched his own country destroyed, he declares Muslims will never forget, never forgive those involved, never again trust politicians easily, and never stop working for reform, and he says Muslims in the West carry special responsibility because they can speak. His first reminder comes from the Quran's account of Badr: committed believers argued against pursuing Abu Sufyan's caravan, feeling marched to death and saying they did not need the money. Allah's repeated use of 'truth' shows the point was never wealth but refusing to accept oppression; forgiving an oppressor while still oppressed is cowardice, and forgiveness belongs to the one who has reclaimed his right. His second reminder laments the earliest and sharpest drop in Ramadan attendance he has seen, possibly because people relied on his 6,500 count, and urges recommitment to the last ten nights as the Prophet did when he woke his family. Third, fasting removes physical distractions so we can hear the starving soul; a taste of closeness to Allah explains how the righteous lived for so little.

outline.heading: Opening
Six months of genocide
outline.gist: On the 19th of Ramadan, two days after the anniversary of Badr, he first turns to six months of watching what he calls the first genocide ever documented live, as it happens and with everyone's knowledge.

outline.heading: Do you condemn the resistance?
outline.gist: That early question now sounds absurd. It was a tactic: set the range of acceptable opinion between A and B, and make every guest answer it before anyone could speak of children pulled from rubble or doctors killed in operating rooms.

outline.heading: A pain only the exiled understand
outline.gist: He lived through war and watched his own country destroyed and taken from him. Everyone in the room comes from a similar legacy; ask why people of so many origins live here.

outline.heading: Never forget, never forgive, never trust
outline.gist: Nobody leaves a country that has justice, rights and dignity. Muslims must state clearly that they will never forget these months, never forgive those involved, and never again easily trust a politician.

outline.heading: Decide now how you will live
outline.gist: We will never stop working for reform and justice. Just before the last ten nights is the best time to decide what will change in your routine, mentality and worldview after Ramadan.

outline.heading: What you produce by treating people as subhuman
outline.gist: He never expected anyone to dare bury 33,000 people under their homes, or the world to accept it. The worst may be yet to come: the children of Gaza will never forget.

outline.heading: The burden of Muslims in the West
outline.gist: Muslims in the West have more than they need and the freedom to speak and advocate, a responsibility to the ummah most do not grasp. We have to reclaim the narrative.

outline.heading: Reminder one: the day truth was separated from falsehood
outline.gist: The first reminder comes from the Badr verses he recited, the day of criterion when the two groups met (8:41).

outline.heading: The Quran tells Badr differently
outline.gist: He taught Badr for years as the seerah books tell it, until he read the Quran's own account. 'Just as your Lord brought you out of your home' links it to the dispute over spoils that opens the surah.

outline.heading: Committed believers who disliked the pursuit
outline.gist: Allah says a group of believers, not hypocrites, disliked going out. The Prophet knew Abu Sufyan's caravan was returning from Damascus to Makkah and where it would pass.

outline.heading: The caravan carried what was theirs
outline.gist: Its wealth came from the homes and possessions the emigrants left in Makkah, which Quraysh sold and traded. The Prophet said to go and take back what was rightfully theirs; many argued against it.

outline.heading: Marched toward death
outline.gist: Some felt driven to their deaths: no one takes on Quraysh, with its army, resources and allies. They said they did not need the money, since Allah had given them better in Madinah.

outline.heading: Allah wanted truth established
outline.gist: Promised the caravan or victory, they hoped for the unarmed group, but Allah willed to establish truth and expose falsehood though the criminals dislike it. Count the word truth: six times in a few verses.

outline.heading: Never about the money: refuse oppression
outline.gist: These were their rights. Take back what is yours, then gift it back if you do not want it. Oppression must be named day after day, whether a hundred years or a thousand pass.

outline.heading: Forgiving while oppressed is cowardice
outline.gist: The principle covers oppression of anyone. The companions briefly had tunnel vision about the caravan. Forgiveness belongs to the one who has reclaimed his right; that is the lesson of the day of criterion.

outline.heading: Badr applied to Palestine and the Muslim world
outline.gist: Speaking for truth must be applied to the Palestinians and to the rights trampled across almost every Muslim-majority country for a century; we refuse to stop naming falsehood.

outline.heading: If this does not wake you, nothing will
outline.gist: What is missing is full commitment; we grew too comfortable. If these six months are not a wake-up call to live differently, nothing ever will be.

outline.heading: Reminder two: the earliest drop he has seen
outline.gist: He had meant to complain: attendance fell earlier and faster than ever across the city, perhaps because people heard his 6,500 count and assumed others would come, like a banquet where everyone brings water.

outline.heading: Atrocity moves people one way or the other
outline.gist: With images of starving children from the Holy Land everywhere, people either come closer to Allah or drift away; nothing stays the same.

outline.heading: Interlude
The Prophet woke his family for the last ten nights
outline.gist: He let Aisha sleep through Ramadan nights, but when the last ten came he woke her: out of love he would not let her waste them. If your Ramadan has not gone well, it is not too late.

outline.heading: Reminder three: why we stop eating and drinking
outline.gist: Eating, drinking and intimacy are deeply physical. In a month when Paradise opens and Allah calls hearts, He removes them by day so the spirit is heightened.

outline.heading: Your soul starves too
outline.gist: Listen to the voice inside: your soul is starving, like the people of Gaza, because it is not properly connected to its Lord. Starved, it shrivels and the ego takes over your intentions and deeds.

outline.heading: A fulfilment nothing compares to
outline.gist: Respond to your soul and you will find a fulfilment so deep you would work day and night for it.

outline.heading: Stories he once thought exaggerated
outline.gist: As a child he doubted accounts of the righteous who worked all day, prayed all night and died leaving nothing to happy families. One taste of closeness to Allah made them make sense.

outline.heading: Earn, but not for yourself
outline.gist: Someone who constantly feels that closeness does not care what the world offers. Work and become rich, then pour it into good; for yourself, look forward only to Allah.

outline.heading: Outro

In Ramadan the gates of Paradise are opened, the gates of Hell closed and the devils chained

Media demand that Muslims condemn the resistance
Distrust of politicians

takeaways: Decide before the last ten nights how your life will change after Ramadan to help prevent such atrocities
Keep naming oppression against Palestinians and anyone else, however long it lasts
Treat reclaiming rights as a matter of principle, not money; forgive only once the right is restored
Return to the masjid and commit fully to the last ten nights, waking your family
Use the fast to listen to your soul and feed it through closeness to Allah

59:24.ar: هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُ ٱلۡبَارِئُ ٱلۡمُصَوِّرُۖ لَهُ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ يُسَبِّحُ لَهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۖ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
59:24.en: He is Allah, the Creator, the Shaper out of naught, the Fashioner. His are the most beautiful names. All that is in the heavens and the earth glorifieth Him, and He is the Mighty, the Wise

39:62.ar: ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲۖ وَهُوَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَكِيلࣱ‏
39:62.en: Allah is Creator of all things, and He is Guardian over all things

7:54.ar: إِنَّ رَبَّكُمُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ فِي سِتَّةِ أَيَّامࣲ ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡعَرۡشِۖ يُغۡشِي ٱلَّيۡلَ ٱلنَّهَارَ يَطۡلُبُهُۥ حَثِيثࣰ ا وَٱلشَّمۡسَ وَٱلۡقَمَرَ وَٱلنُّجُومَ مُسَخَّرَٰتِۭ بِأَمۡرِهِۦٓۗ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ وَٱلۡأَمۡرُۗ تَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ رَبُّ ٱلۡعَٰلَمِينَ
7:54.en: Lo! your Lord is Allah Who created the heavens and the earth in six Days, then mounted He the Throne. He covereth the night with the day, which is in haste to follow it, and hath made the sun and the moon and the stars subservient by His command. His verily is all creation and commandment. Blessed be Allah, the Lord of the Worlds

23:12.ar: وَلَقَدۡ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡإِنسَٰنَ مِن سُلَٰلَةࣲ مِّن طِينࣲ‏
23:12.en: Verily We created man from a product of wet earth

23:13.ar: ثُمَّ جَعَلۡنَٰهُ نُطۡفَةࣰ فِي قَرَارࣲ مَّكِينࣲ‏
23:13.en: Then placed him as a drop (of seed) in a safe lodging

23:14.ar: ثُمَّ خَلَقۡنَا ٱلنُّطۡفَةَ عَلَقَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡعَلَقَةَ مُضۡغَةࣰ فَخَلَقۡنَا ٱلۡمُضۡغَةَ عِظَٰمࣰ ا فَكَسَوۡنَا ٱلۡعِظَٰمَ لَحۡمࣰ ا ثُمَّ أَنشَأۡنَٰهُ خَلۡقًا ءَاخَرَۚ فَتَبَارَكَ ٱللَّهُ أَحۡسَنُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقِينَ
23:14.en: Then fashioned We the drop a clot, then fashioned We the clot a little lump, then fashioned We the little lump bones, then clothed the bones with flesh, and then produced it as another creation. So blessed be Allah, the Best of creators

2:21.ar: يَٰٓأَيُّهَا ٱلنَّاسُ ٱعۡبُدُواْ رَبَّكُمُ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَكُمۡ وَٱلَّذِينَ مِن قَبۡلِكُمۡ لَعَلَّكُمۡ تَتَّقُونَ
2:21.en: O mankind! worship your Lord, Who hath created you and those before you, so that ye may ward off (evil)

36:81.ar: أَوَلَيۡسَ ٱلَّذِي خَلَقَ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَ بِقَٰدِرٍ عَلَىٰٓ أَن يَخۡلُقَ مِثۡلَهُمۚ بَلَىٰ وَهُوَ ٱلۡخَلَّٰقُ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ
36:81.en: Is not He Who created the heavens and the earth Able to create the like of them? Aye, that He is! for He is the All-Wise Creator

76:1.ar: هَلۡ أَتَىٰ عَلَى ٱلۡإِنسَٰنِ حِينࣱ مِّنَ ٱلدَّهۡرِ لَمۡ يَكُن شَيۡـࣰٔ ا مَّذۡكُورًا
76:1.en: Hath there come upon man (ever) any period of time in which he was a thing unremembered

52:35.ar: أَمۡ خُلِقُواْ مِنۡ غَيۡرِ شَيۡءٍ أَمۡ هُمُ ٱلۡخَٰلِقُونَ
52:35.en: Or were they created out of naught? Or are they the creators

52:36.ar: أَمۡ خَلَقُواْ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ
52:36.en: Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Nay, but they are sure of nothing

29:20.ar: قُلۡ سِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَٱنظُرُواْ كَيۡفَ بَدَأَ ٱلۡخَلۡقَۚ ثُمَّ ٱللَّهُ يُنشِئُ ٱلنَّشۡأَةَ ٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ قَدِيرࣱ‏
29:20.en: Say (O Muhammad): Travel in the land and see how He originated creation, then Allah bringeth forth the later growth. Lo! Allah is Able to do all things

71:17.ar: وَٱللَّهُ أَنۢبَتَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ نَبَاتࣰ ا
71:17.en: And Allah hath caused you to grow as a growth from the earth

56:58.en: Have ye seen that which ye emit

56:59.en: Do ye create it or are We the Creator

30:27.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِي يَبۡدَؤُاْ ٱلۡخَلۡقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَهُوَ أَهۡوَنُ عَلَيۡهِۚ وَلَهُ ٱلۡمَثَلُ ٱلۡأَعۡلَىٰ فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَزِيزُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
30:27.en: He it is Who produceth creation, then reproduceth it, and it is easier for Him. His is the Sublime Similitude in the heavens and the earth. He is the Mighty, the Wise

13:16.ar: قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ اۚ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ أَمۡ هَلۡ تَسۡتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتُ وَٱلنُّورُۗ أَمۡ جَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلۡقِهِۦ فَتَشَٰبَهَ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّٰرُ
13:16.en: Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt? Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty

31:11.ar: هَٰذَا خَلۡقُ ٱللَّهِ فَأَرُونِي مَاذَا خَلَقَ ٱلَّذِينَ مِن دُونِهِۦۚ بَلِ ٱلظَّٰلِمُونَ فِي ضَلَٰلࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
31:11.en: This is the Creation of Allah. Now show me that which those (ye worship) beside Him have created. Nay, but the wrong-doers are in error manifest

96GhzDQb2l8.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari' and Al-Musawwir (Names of Creation)
96GhzDQb2l8.one_line: The names of creation: why Al-Khaliq is deeply spiritual, what the Quran says about how creation began, and what science cannot answer.
96GhzDQb2l8.summary: Opening the category of names related to creation, he takes Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari' and Al-Musawwir together. He argues people treat these names as mechanical when the bond between Creator and creation is more intimate than that between a parent and child, since nothing of us comes from anyone but Allah. He separates the meanings: bringing something from nothing, giving it life, and giving it a form that serves a purpose. He walks through verses on creation, the hadith that Allah existed when nothing else did, a teacher's reading of the throne over 'matter', the order of creation from the pen onward, and Jubayr ibn Mut'im's shock on hearing Surat al-Tur. He stresses that the Quran commands people to travel and study how creation began, that the time creation took is Allah's business, and that the image of a deity zapping things into being is medieval, not Islamic. Science studies what lies between the origins but never asks how nothing became matter, how matter became life, or why life wants to keep living. He closes with two duties: respect and appreciate Allah's creation and walk humbly in it, and act as a caring steward over everything placed under human care.

outline.heading: Names of creation: three names in one session
outline.gist: He introduces the category of creation and the three names Al-Khaliq, Al-Bari' and Al-Musawwir, noting how often each appears in the Quran.

outline.heading: The most intimate bond: Creator and creation
outline.gist: People see Al-Khaliq as mechanical, but the Creator's bond with what He made is closer than a parent's bond with a child, who carries only half of each parent.

outline.heading: Khaliq, Bari' and Musawwir distinguished
outline.gist: Bringing into existence from nothing, granting life, and giving a form that serves a function and purpose, with Al-Khaliq as the umbrella name over everything.

outline.heading: Creation and command: the two books
outline.gist: The universe is Allah's open book and revelation His written book; both come from one source so they never contradict.

outline.heading: Stages of the embryo: creation as transformation
outline.gist: The verse on embryonic stages shows that creating can also mean transforming something into a different creation, ending with Allah as the best of creators.

outline.heading: Al-Khallaq: the One who keeps creating
outline.gist: Verses calling people to worship their Creator and asserting He can recreate the heavens and earth; He creates continuously, including things we have never encountered.

outline.heading: How it began: Allah and nothing besides Him
outline.gist: The hadith of the delegation asking how creation began, and a teacher's view that the throne being over 'water' points to Allah's control over the first matter.

outline.heading: A time when man was not a thing mentioned
outline.gist: Humans were not the first creation; something cannot be described before it exists.

outline.heading: Jubayr ibn Mut'im hears Surat al-Tur
outline.gist: The verses asking whether people were created from nothing or created themselves shook Jubayr; deniers simply prefer to live in ambiguity.

outline.heading: The order of creation: pen, decree, cosmos, jinn, humans
outline.gist: After matter came the pen that wrote all that would happen in time, then the universe, the jinn from smokeless fire, and finally human beings.

outline.heading: Many words for human origins are symbolic, not contradictory
outline.gist: The Quran describes humans as from dust, clay and water in different phrases; it is not an anthropology book but tells you to go and learn.

outline.heading: Commanded to study how creation began
outline.gist: The verse ordering people to travel the earth and see how He began creation, and the image of humans grown from the earth like plants, suggest gradual creation that can be discovered.

outline.heading: How long creation took is Allah's business
outline.gist: Whether a second or billions of years makes no difference; the bearded deity zapping things into being is a medieval church idea, never the Muslim view, and science shows the method.

outline.heading: Verses challenging people to see who creates
outline.gist: Do you create the fluid you emit, He begins creation and repeats it and the second time is easier, and did partners create anything like His creation.

outline.heading: This is Allah's creation: show me what others made
outline.gist: The closing verse of challenge: no one else has created anything.

outline.heading: Science cannot ask how nothing became something
outline.gist: Science starts from the first matter after the Big Bang; where matter came from is a philosophical question, and lifeless matter cannot produce living beings.

outline.heading: From matter to life: a mystery no one studies
outline.gist: Drawing on his work in oncology, he describes how little we understand even of one cell; science studies how life works, not how life first came from non-life.

outline.heading: Why does life want to live?
outline.gist: Every living thing fights to survive and resists death at the last moment; no one explains where that programming of purpose came from.

outline.heading: Three beginnings beyond our grasp
outline.gist: We study everything between existence, life and purpose but not their beginnings, which is exactly what these names are about and why they are spiritual.

outline.heading: Living the names: respect His creation
outline.gist: Appreciate and acknowledge the beauty of what Allah made, as the Quran keeps telling you to look, and walk the earth humbly as a creation inside His creation.

outline.heading: Living the names: be a caregiver and steward
outline.gist: Humans were made more capable and given stewardship, so they are responsible for the wellbeing of everything around them.

outline.heading: Outro

Jubayr ibn Mut'im heard the Prophet recite Surat al-Tur in Maghrib and said his heart almost flew from his chest at the verses on creation
The first thing Allah created was the pen, which was commanded to write everything that will happen until the end of time

7:186.ar: مَن يُضۡلِلِ ٱللَّهُ فَلَا هَادِيَ لَهُۥۚ وَيَذَرُهُمۡ فِي طُغۡيَٰنِهِمۡ يَعۡمَهُونَ

33:4.en: Allah hath not assigned unto any man two hearts within his body, nor hath He made your wives whom ye declare (to be your mothers) your mothers, nor hath He made those whom ye claim (to be your sons) your sons. 49:17.en: They make it a favour unto thee (Muhammad) that they have surrendered (unto Him). Say: Deem not your Surrender a favour unto me; but Allah doth confer a favour on you, inasmuch as He hath led you to the Faith, if ye are earnest

7:43.ar: وَنَزَعۡنَا مَا فِي صُدُورِهِم مِّنۡ غِلࣲّ تَجۡرِي مِن تَحۡتِهِمُ ٱلۡأَنۡهَٰرُۖ وَقَالُواْ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ لِلَّهِ ٱلَّذِي هَدَىٰنَا لِهَٰذَا وَمَا كُنَّا لِنَهۡتَدِيَ لَوۡلَآ أَنۡ هَدَىٰنَا ٱللَّهُۖ لَقَدۡ جَآءَتۡ رُسُلُ رَبِّنَا بِٱلۡحَقِّۖ وَنُودُوٓاْ أَن تِلۡكُمُ ٱلۡجَنَّةُ أُورِثۡتُمُوهَا بِمَا كُنتُمۡ تَعۡمَلُونَ

10:35.ar: قُلۡ هَلۡ مِن شُرَكَآئِكُم مَّن يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلۡحَقِّۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ يَهۡدِي لِلۡحَقِّۗ أَفَمَن يَهۡدِيٓ إِلَى ٱلۡحَقِّ أَحَقُّ أَن يُتَّبَعَ أَمَّن لَّا يَهِدِّيٓ إِلَّآ أَن يُهۡدَىٰۖ فَمَا لَكُمۡ كَيۡفَ تَحۡكُمُونَ
10:35.en: Say: Is there of your partners (whom ye ascribe unto Allah) one that leadeth to the Truth? Say: Allah leadeth to the Truth. Is He Who leadeth to the Truth more deserving that He should be followed, or he who findeth not the way unless he (himself) be guided. What aileth you? How judge ye

30:52.ar: فَإِنَّكَ لَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلۡمَوۡتَىٰ وَلَا تُسۡمِعُ ٱلصُّمَّ ٱلدُّعَآءَ إِذَا وَلَّوۡاْ مُدۡبِرِينَ

30:53.ar: وَمَآ أَنتَ بِهَٰدِ ٱلۡعُمۡيِ عَن ضَلَٰلَتِهِمۡۖ إِن تُسۡمِعُ إِلَّا مَن يُؤۡمِنُ بِـَٔايَٰتِنَا فَهُم مُّسۡلِمُونَ

28:56.en: Lo! thou (O Muhammad) guidest not whom thou lovest, but Allah guideth whom He will. And He is Best Aware of those who walk aright

10:100.ar: وَمَا كَانَ لِنَفۡسٍ أَن تُؤۡمِنَ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِ ٱللَّهِۚ وَيَجۡعَلُ ٱلرِّجۡسَ عَلَى ٱلَّذِينَ لَا يَعۡقِلُونَ
10:100.en: It is not for any soul to believe save by the permission of Allah. He hath set uncleanness upon those who have no sense

41:33.ar: وَمَنۡ أَحۡسَنُ قَوۡلࣰ ا مِّمَّن دَعَآ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ وَعَمِلَ صَٰلِحࣰ ا وَقَالَ إِنَّنِي مِنَ ٱلۡمُسۡلِمِينَ
41:33.en: And who is better in speech than him who prayeth unto his Lord and doeth right, and saith: Lo! I am of those who are muslims (surrender unto Him)

w1SUx2Z7naU.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Hadi (The Grantor of Guidance)
w1SUx2Z7naU.one_line: Al-Hadi: four levels of guidance, why we cannot guide those we love, how Umar, Ibn Salam and Dimad were guided, and becoming a means of guidance.
w1SUx2Z7naU.summary: Within the names of positive control he chooses Al-Hadi and lays out four levels of guidance. First is general guidance: Allah gave everything its form and then guided it to its function, from immune cells to ants, and humans alone need extended coaching. Second is guidance to faith, which awakens what the soul already knows from the primordial covenant and its innate sense of right and wrong. Third, Allah increases the guided in guidance, and fourth, He guides the people of Paradise to it, whose first words are praise for that guidance. Everyone has a unique story of how they reached the masjid, but no one can force guidance even on those they love, as the Prophet's grief over Abu Talib shows. Guidance comes in different ways: gradually for Umar over years, in a single look for Abdullah ibn Salam, and through words for Dimad, who came to treat the Prophet and accepted Islam after hearing his opening praise. Along the way he urges families to do ruqyah for one another rather than paying practitioners. Because we ask for guidance at least seventeen times daily, he stresses that it is an endless path and our conduct should match the request. He asks for gratitude without arrogance, for being the means of others' guidance, and for letting actions guide more than words.

outline.heading: Names of positive and correctional control
outline.gist: These paired categories hold names with opposite meanings that are best studied together; he picks a name in each without a well-known opposite.

outline.heading: Al-Hadi in the Quran
outline.gist: Whomever Allah leaves astray has no guide, every nation has a guide, and Allah speaks the truth and guides the way.

outline.heading: What guidance means
outline.gist: Allah guides His creation to what serves its interest and lets it function, whether in general life, knowledge or faith.

outline.heading: First level: general guidance of all creation
outline.gist: He gave everything its form and guided it; immune cells, ants and newborn animals find their function, and its failure, like autoimmune disease, shows how vital it is; humans alone need long coaching.

outline.heading: Second level: guidance to faith
outline.gist: Iman is a favour Allah bestows, not a personal achievement.

outline.heading: The soul knows right from wrong
outline.gist: Allah inspired the soul with its wickedness and righteousness, and every person has insight into himself.

outline.heading: The primordial covenant
outline.gist: Allah addressed all of Adam's offspring, who testified to His lordship, so that no one can blame indifference or their ancestors; guidance awakens what we always knew.

outline.heading: Third level: increase in guidance
outline.gist: The Quran guides to what is most upright, and Allah increases the guided, like the youth of the cave, in guidance.

outline.heading: Fourth level: guided to Paradise
outline.gist: The first words of the people of Jannah are praise to Allah who guided them to it.

outline.heading: Who is more worthy of being followed
outline.gist: Allah guides to the truth, while false partners cannot even find guidance unless guided.

outline.heading: Your own story of guidance
outline.gist: Everyone sitting in the masjid reached it through layers of guidance only they know.

outline.heading: You cannot guide those you love: Abu Talib
outline.gist: We can only offer words to those seeking; the Prophet's lifelong pain over his uncle shows guidance is Allah's to give.

outline.heading: Guided gradually: Umar ibn al-Khattab
outline.gist: Over years, a steadfast servant girl, the Quran at the Ka'bah, a fleeing mother and finally his sister's scroll turned his heart.

outline.heading: Guided by a look: Abdullah ibn Salam
outline.gist: The rabbi rehearsed questions to expose the Prophet, but one look at his face was enough.

outline.heading: Do ruqyah for your own family
outline.gist: Paying practitioners for ruqyah is a pre-Islamic habit; family members can recite the known verses and duas for one another.

outline.heading: Guided by words: Dimad
outline.gist: Dimad came to treat the Prophet for madness, heard his opening praise three times, declared it beyond any poetry or sorcery and accepted Islam with his people.

outline.heading: Asking for guidance seventeen times a day
outline.gist: Anyone recording our daily words would conclude we are obsessed with guidance, since we ask for it in every rakah of Al-Fatihah.

outline.heading: Guidance has no end
outline.gist: Closeness to Allah is not physical, so guidance is infinite; since we ask for it constantly, our lives should show we want it.

outline.heading: Living the name: gratitude
outline.gist: No soul believes except by Allah's will, though He opens hearts according to sincerity, so be grateful for guidance.

outline.heading: Never use guidance to look down on others
outline.gist: Guidance is a gift second only to life, not grounds for arrogance or labelling people.

outline.heading: Living the name: be a means of guidance
outline.gist: Allah guides mostly through people, as through the prophets; none speaks better than one who calls to Allah and lives righteously.

outline.heading: Living the name: actions guide better than words
outline.gist: A successful, impactful life as a good Muslim reaches far more people than lectures can.

outline.heading: Better than all the riches of the world
outline.gist: That Allah guides one person through you is better than owning the world's wealth.

outline.heading: Bringing back the one who strayed
outline.gist: Helping a lost servant return to Allah is like telling Him you will take care of the one He loves; nothing is more beautiful.
