contemporary: Constant scrolling and quick online lookups crowding out reflection
A heavy habit in the Muslim community of copying the past without scrutiny
takeaways: Obey clearly established commands even when you cannot see their wisdom
Admit your mistakes quickly and accept the blame, as the prophets did
Sift inherited customs respectfully: keep the good, let go of the rest and keep making dua for your parents
Set aside real time to contemplate ideas, Allah and your own life
Let worry about the Hereafter at least balance worldly worries, and keep your spirit connected to Allah while awake

6:59.ar: ۞وَعِندَهُۥ مَفَاتِحُ ٱلۡغَيۡبِ لَا يَعۡلَمُهَآ إِلَّا هُوَۚ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡبَرِّ وَٱلۡبَحۡرِۚ وَمَا تَسۡقُطُ مِن وَرَقَةٍ إِلَّا يَعۡلَمُهَا وَلَا حَبَّةࣲ فِي ظُلُمَٰتِ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَلَا رَطۡبࣲ وَلَا يَابِسٍ إِلَّا فِي كِتَٰبࣲ مُّبِينࣲ‏
6:59.en: And with Him are the keys of the Invisible. None but He knoweth them. And He knoweth what is in the land and the sea. Not a leaf falleth but He knoweth it, not a grain amid the darkness of the earth, naught of wet or dry but (it is noted) in a clear record

31:34.ar: إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عِندَهُۥ عِلۡمُ ٱلسَّاعَةِ وَيُنَزِّلُ ٱلۡغَيۡثَ وَيَعۡلَمُ مَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡحَامِۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسࣱ مَّاذَا تَكۡسِبُ غَدࣰ اۖ وَمَا تَدۡرِي نَفۡسُۢ بِأَيِّ أَرۡضࣲ تَمُوتُۚ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَلِيمٌ خَبِيرُۢ
31:34.en: Lo! Allah! With Him is knowledge of the Hour. He sendeth down the rain, and knoweth that which is in the wombs. No soul knoweth what it will earn to-morrow, and no soul knoweth in what land it will die. Lo! Allah is Knower, Aware

53:32.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَجۡتَنِبُونَ كَبَٰٓئِرَ ٱلۡإِثۡمِ وَٱلۡفَوَٰحِشَ إِلَّا ٱللَّمَمَۚ إِنَّ رَبَّكَ وَٰسِعُ ٱلۡمَغۡفِرَةِۚ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِكُمۡ إِذۡ أَنشَأَكُم مِّنَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَإِذۡ أَنتُمۡ أَجِنَّةࣱ فِي بُطُونِ أُمَّهَٰتِكُمۡۖ فَلَا تُزَكُّوٓاْ أَنفُسَكُمۡۖ هُوَ أَعۡلَمُ بِمَنِ ٱتَّقَىٰٓ
53:32.en: Those who avoid enormities of sin and abominations, save the unwilled offences - (for them) lo! thy Lord is of vast mercy. He is Best Aware of you (from the time) when He created you from the earth, and when ye were hidden in the bellies of your mothers. Therefor ascribe not purity unto yourselves. He is Best Aware of him who wardeth off (evil)

2:30.ar: وَإِذۡ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ إِنِّي جَاعِلࣱ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ خَلِيفَةࣰۖ قَالُوٓاْ أَتَجۡعَلُ فِيهَا مَن يُفۡسِدُ فِيهَا وَيَسۡفِكُ ٱلدِّمَآءَ وَنَحۡنُ نُسَبِّحُ بِحَمۡدِكَ وَنُقَدِّسُ لَكَۖ قَالَ إِنِّيٓ أَعۡلَمُ مَا لَا تَعۡلَمُونَ
2:30.en: And when thy Lord said unto the angels: Lo! I am about to place a viceroy in the earth, they said: Wilt thou place therein one who will do harm therein and will shed blood, while we, we hymn Thy praise and sanctify Thee? He said: Surely I know that which ye know not

2:31.ar: وَعَلَّمَ ءَادَمَ ٱلۡأَسۡمَآءَ كُلَّهَا ثُمَّ عَرَضَهُمۡ عَلَى ٱلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ فَقَالَ أَنۢبِـُٔونِي بِأَسۡمَآءِ هَٰٓؤُلَآءِ إِن كُنتُمۡ صَٰدِقِينَ
2:31.en: And He taught Adam all the names, then showed them to the angels, saying: Inform Me of the names of these, if ye are truthful

2:32.ar: قَالُواْ سُبۡحَٰنَكَ لَا عِلۡمَ لَنَآ إِلَّا مَا عَلَّمۡتَنَآۖ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡعَلِيمُ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ
2:32.en: They said: Be glorified! We have no knowledge saving that which Thou hast taught us. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Knower, the Wise

96:1.en: Read: In the name of thy Lord Who createth

40:7.ar: ٱلَّذِينَ يَحۡمِلُونَ ٱلۡعَرۡشَ وَمَنۡ حَوۡلَهُۥ يُسَبِّحُونَ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّهِمۡ وَيُؤۡمِنُونَ بِهِۦ وَيَسۡتَغۡفِرُونَ لِلَّذِينَ ءَامَنُواْۖ رَبَّنَا وَسِعۡتَ كُلَّ شَيۡءࣲ رَّحۡمَةࣰ وَعِلۡمࣰ ا فَٱغۡفِرۡ لِلَّذِينَ تَابُواْ وَٱتَّبَعُواْ سَبِيلَكَ وَقِهِمۡ عَذَابَ ٱلۡجَحِيمِ
40:7.en: Those who bear the Throne, and all who are round about it, hymn the praises of their Lord and believe in Him and ask forgiveness for those who believe (saying): Our Lord! Thou comprehendest all things in mercy and knowledge, therefor forgive those who repent and follow Thy way. Ward off from them the punishment of hell

34:2.ar: يَعۡلَمُ مَا يَلِجُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَمَا يَخۡرُجُ مِنۡهَا وَمَا يَنزِلُ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَمَا يَعۡرُجُ فِيهَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلرَّحِيمُ ٱلۡغَفُورُ
34:2.en: He knoweth that which goeth into the earth and that which cometh forth from it, and that descendeth from the heaven and that which ascendeth into it. He is the Merciful, the Forgiving

18:65.ar: فَوَجَدَا عَبۡدࣰ ا مِّنۡ عِبَادِنَآ ءَاتَيۡنَٰهُ رَحۡمَةࣰ مِّنۡ عِندِنَا وَعَلَّمۡنَٰهُ مِن لَّدُنَّا عِلۡمࣰ ا
18:65.en: Then found they one of Our slaves, unto whom We had given mercy from Us, and had taught him knowledge from Our presence

28:69.ar: وَرَبُّكَ يَعۡلَمُ مَا تُكِنُّ صُدُورُهُمۡ وَمَا يُعۡلِنُونَ
28:69.en: And thy Lord knoweth what their breasts conceal, and what they publish

28:70.ar: وَهُوَ ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۖ لَهُ ٱلۡحَمۡدُ فِي ٱلۡأُولَىٰ وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةِۖ وَلَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَإِلَيۡهِ تُرۡجَعُونَ
28:70.en: And He is Allah; there is no Allah save Him. His is all praise in the former and the latter (state), and His is the command, and unto Him ye will be brought back

28:71.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِضِيَآءٍۚ أَفَلَا تَسۡمَعُونَ
28:71.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made night everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you light? Will ye not then hear

28:72.ar: قُلۡ أَرَءَيۡتُمۡ إِن جَعَلَ ٱللَّهُ عَلَيۡكُمُ ٱلنَّهَارَ سَرۡمَدًا إِلَىٰ يَوۡمِ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ مَنۡ إِلَٰهٌ غَيۡرُ ٱللَّهِ يَأۡتِيكُم بِلَيۡلࣲ تَسۡكُنُونَ فِيهِۚ أَفَلَا تُبۡصِرُونَ
28:72.en: Say: Have ye thought, if Allah made day everlasting for you till the Day of Resurrection, who is a god beside Allah who could bring you night wherein ye rest? Will ye not then see

28:73.ar: وَمِن رَّحۡمَتِهِۦ جَعَلَ لَكُمُ ٱلَّيۡلَ وَٱلنَّهَارَ لِتَسۡكُنُواْ فِيهِ وَلِتَبۡتَغُواْ مِن فَضۡلِهِۦ وَلَعَلَّكُمۡ تَشۡكُرُونَ
28:73.en: Of His mercy hath He appointed for you night and day, that therein ye may rest, and that ye may seek His bounty, and that haply ye may be thankful

3:7.ar: هُوَ ٱلَّذِيٓ أَنزَلَ عَلَيۡكَ ٱلۡكِتَٰبَ مِنۡهُ ءَايَٰتࣱ مُّحۡكَمَٰتٌ هُنَّ أُمُّ ٱلۡكِتَٰبِ وَأُخَرُ مُتَشَٰبِهَٰتࣱۖ فَأَمَّا ٱلَّذِينَ فِي قُلُوبِهِمۡ زَيۡغࣱ فَيَتَّبِعُونَ مَا تَشَٰبَهَ مِنۡهُ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ ٱلۡفِتۡنَةِ وَٱبۡتِغَآءَ تَأۡوِيلِهِۦۖ وَمَا يَعۡلَمُ تَأۡوِيلَهُۥٓ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُۗ وَٱلرَّٰسِخُونَ فِي ٱلۡعِلۡمِ يَقُولُونَ ءَامَنَّا بِهِۦ كُلࣱّ مِّنۡ عِندِ رَبِّنَاۗ وَمَا يَذَّكَّرُ إِلَّآ أُوْلُواْ ٱلۡأَلۡبَٰبِ
3:7.en: He it is Who hath revealed unto thee (Muhammad) the Scripture wherein are clear revelations - they are the substance of the Book - and others (which are) allegorical. But those in whose hearts is doubt pursue, forsooth, that which is allegorical seeking (to cause) dissension by seeking to explain it. None knoweth its explanation save Allah. And those who are of sound instruction say: We believe therein; the whole is from our Lord; but only men of understanding really heed

3:8.ar: رَبَّنَا لَا تُزِغۡ قُلُوبَنَا بَعۡدَ إِذۡ هَدَيۡتَنَا وَهَبۡ لَنَا مِن لَّدُنكَ رَحۡمَةًۚ إِنَّكَ أَنتَ ٱلۡوَهَّابُ
3:8.en: Our Lord! Cause not our hearts to stray after Thou hast guided us, and bestow upon us mercy from Thy Presence. Lo! Thou, only Thou, art the Bestower

35:28.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ وَٱلدَّوَآبِّ وَٱلۡأَنۡعَٰمِ مُخۡتَلِفٌ أَلۡوَٰنُهُۥ كَذَٰلِكَۗ إِنَّمَا يَخۡشَى ٱللَّهَ مِنۡ عِبَادِهِ ٱلۡعُلَمَٰٓؤُاْۗ إِنَّ ٱللَّهَ عَزِيزٌ غَفُورٌ
35:28.en: And of men and beasts and cattle, in like manner, divers hues? The erudite among His bondmen fear Allah alone. Lo! Allah is Mighty, Forgiving

mshxcXvBTeI.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Alim (The All-Knowing)
mshxcXvBTeI.one_line: Al-Alim: knowledge paired with wisdom and mercy, foreknowledge without compulsion, knowledge as strength and ignorance as the enemy, and becoming lifelong learners.
mshxcXvBTeI.summary: Al-Alim, an umbrella name appearing about 170 times, is one he says reason reaches even without revelation. It most often pairs with Al-Hakim, reassuring us that infinite knowledge is used wisely. He reads the verses on the keys of the unseen, the five things only Allah knows, and the command not to claim purity since Allah knows us from the womb. In the creation of Adam, the angels' objection turned to praise once Adam articulated the names, because they saw a new capacity to process, connect and build on knowledge; hence Allah taught bayan and the first revelation was Read, meaning to comprehend. He then draws four points. Allah encompasses all things with mercy and knowledge, and knowledge without mercy is catastrophic, from bombs to exploitation. His knowledge of the future does not compel it, since knowing is not an impactful attribute and Allah is outside the time He created; a god who could be surprised could be beaten. Knowledge is strength, and endless learning may be the greatest joy of Jannah, though schooling conditions people to find it dull. Ignorance is the ultimate enemy, turning power into oppression and religion into extremism. He urges people to become lifelong seekers of knowledge and to spread it, since rulers keep populations distracted and uninformed.

outline.heading: An umbrella name, 170 times in the Quran
outline.gist: Al-Alim is extremely general, gathering many narrower names, and appears far more often than the names covered earlier.

outline.heading: A name reason reaches on its own
outline.gist: Omniscience follows naturally from the idea of God; it appears as Alim, Allam al-Ghuyub and Knower of the unseen and seen.

outline.heading: Paired with many names, most of all Al-Hakim
outline.gist: Al-Alim accompanies over twelve names to clarify them, and most often appears with the All-Wise.

outline.heading: Knowledge guided by wisdom
outline.gist: Knowledge can harm unless joined to wisdom, so pairing it with Al-Hakim reassures us it is used for good.

outline.heading: The keys of the unseen
outline.gist: Not a leaf falls nor a seed lies in the earth's darkness, wet or dry, except that He knows it.

outline.heading: The five things only Allah knows
outline.gist: Knowledge of the Hour, rain, what is in wombs, what one will earn tomorrow and where one will die.

outline.heading: Do not claim purity for yourselves
outline.gist: He knew you from the earth and the womb, so do not boast of goodness; He knows who has taqwa.

outline.heading: The Prophet's dua describing Allah's knowledge
outline.gist: He knows the weight of mountains, the water in the seas, every leaf and raindrop, and what lies at the base of every mountain.

outline.heading: Adam: the angels object, Allah teaches the names
outline.gist: The angels feared another corrupting creature; Allah said He knows what they do not and taught Adam the names.

outline.heading: The angels' reaction changes
outline.gist: The angels, free of envy or agenda, praised Allah once Adam spoke, recognising knowledge only comes from Him.

outline.heading: Adam's unique potential to learn
outline.gist: Adam could process information, connect dots and build conclusions, something the angels had never seen.

outline.heading: He taught the Quran and taught man bayan
outline.gist: The ability to articulate lets knowledge pass to others who never experienced it, which is the basis of learning.

outline.heading: Iqra: read as comprehend
outline.gist: The first revealed command means to understand and read situations between the lines, not only to recite.

outline.heading: First point: encompassing all with mercy and knowledge
outline.gist: The angels' prayer says Allah encompasses everything with mercy and knowledge, attributes that reach all things equally, unlike provision or power.

outline.heading: Knowledge always beside mercy
outline.gist: Examples where knowledge and mercy appear together, including Khidr, given mercy and then knowledge.

outline.heading: Knowledge without mercy is catastrophic
outline.gist: The firmly grounded in knowledge ask for mercy, because knowledge without it builds bombs, exploits people and ruins the environment.

outline.heading: Second point: foreknowledge is not compulsion
outline.gist: His will and His knowledge are distinct; knowing something does not affect its existence, so His knowing the future does not force it.

outline.heading: Allah is outside time
outline.gist: Humans predict only what is programmed, but Allah created time and speaks of past and future alike, so He knows our free choices.

outline.heading: What came before Allah is a meaningless question
outline.gist: Before and after are features of created time, so they do not apply to Him.

outline.heading: A god who can be surprised can be beaten
outline.gist: Omniscience is part of what it means to be God, and it leaves our freedom of choice intact.

outline.heading: Third point: knowledge is strength, and the joy of Jannah
outline.gist: His teacher said the greatest joy of Paradise is access to Allah's infinite knowledge; the brain delights in learning more than in physical pleasures.

outline.heading: Schooling made us find knowledge dull
outline.gist: Conditioned to see learning as forced and boring, people step away from the most beautiful thing they have.

outline.heading: Fourth point: ignorance is the ultimate enemy
outline.gist: Ignorance with health breeds bullying, with wealth waste, with religion extremism, with power oppression; hence the pre-Islamic era is named after it.

outline.heading: Living the name: seek knowledge; scholar over worshipper
outline.gist: Be a lifelong learner; the scholar's superiority over the worshipper is like the Prophet's over the least of Muslims.

outline.heading: A path to Jannah made easy
outline.gist: Allah eases the way to Paradise for one who seeks knowledge, who has understood what truly matters.

outline.heading: The inheritance of the prophets and true reverence
outline.gist: Creatures of the sea seek forgiveness for the student, prophets left knowledge not money, and those who know truly revere Allah.

outline.heading: Living the name: spread knowledge
outline.gist: Raising the ummah's baseline of religious and academic knowledge is how it will recover.

outline.heading: Rulers keep people distracted and ignorant
outline.gist: Entertainment and distraction keep populations from asking questions and uncovering corruption.

14:48.ar: يَوۡمَ تُبَدَّلُ ٱلۡأَرۡضُ غَيۡرَ ٱلۡأَرۡضِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُۖ وَبَرَزُواْ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
14:48.en: On the day when the earth will be changed to other than the earth, and the heavens (also will be changed) and they will come forth unto Allah, the One, the Almighty

40:16.ar: يَوۡمَ هُم بَٰرِزُونَۖ لَا يَخۡفَىٰ عَلَى ٱللَّهِ مِنۡهُمۡ شَيۡءࣱۚ لِّمَنِ ٱلۡمُلۡكُ ٱلۡيَوۡمَۖ لِلَّهِ ٱلۡوَٰحِدِ ٱلۡقَهَّارِ
40:16.en: The day when they come forth, nothing of them being hidden from Allah. Whose is the Sovereignty this day? It is Allah's, the One, the Almighty

12:39.ar: يَٰصَٰحِبَيِ ٱلسِّجۡنِ ءَأَرۡبَابࣱ مُّتَفَرِّقُونَ خَيۡرٌ أَمِ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
12:39.en: O my fellow-prisoners! Are divers lords better, or Allah the One, Almighty

13:16.ar: قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ اۚ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ أَمۡ هَلۡ تَسۡتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتُ وَٱلنُّورُۗ أَمۡ جَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلۡقِهِۦ فَتَشَٰبَهَ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّٰرُ
13:16.en: Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt? Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty

38:65.ar: قُلۡ إِنَّمَآ أَنَا۠ مُنذِرࣱۖ وَمَا مِنۡ إِلَٰهٍ إِلَّا ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
38:65.en: Say (unto them, O Muhammad): I am only a warner, and there is no Allah save Allah, the One, the Absolute

39:4.ar: لَّوۡ أَرَادَ ٱللَّهُ أَن يَتَّخِذَ وَلَدࣰ ا لَّٱصۡطَفَىٰ مِمَّا يَخۡلُقُ مَا يَشَآءُۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥۖ هُوَ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّارُ
39:4.en: If Allah had willed to choose a son, He could have chosen what He would of that which He hath created. Be He Glorified! He is Allah, the One, the Absolute

6:61.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦۖ وَيُرۡسِلُ عَلَيۡكُمۡ حَفَظَةً حَتَّىٰٓ إِذَا جَآءَ أَحَدَكُمُ ٱلۡمَوۡتُ تَوَفَّتۡهُ رُسُلُنَا وَهُمۡ لَا يُفَرِّطُونَ
6:61.en: He is the Omnipotent over His slaves. He sendeth guardians over you until, when death cometh unto one of you, Our messengers receive him, and they neglect not

6:62.ar: ثُمَّ رُدُّوٓاْ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ مَوۡلَىٰهُمُ ٱلۡحَقِّۚ أَلَا لَهُ ٱلۡحُكۡمُ وَهُوَ أَسۡرَعُ ٱلۡحَٰسِبِينَ
6:62.en: Then are they restored unto Allah, their Lord, the Just. Surely His is the judgment. And He is the most swift of reckoners

6:18.ar: وَهُوَ ٱلۡقَاهِرُ فَوۡقَ عِبَادِهِۦۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡحَكِيمُ ٱلۡخَبِيرُ
6:18.en: He is the Omnipotent over His slaves, and He is the Wise, the Knower

41:11.ar: ثُمَّ ٱسۡتَوَىٰٓ إِلَى ٱلسَّمَآءِ وَهِيَ دُخَانࣱ فَقَالَ لَهَا وَلِلۡأَرۡضِ ٱئۡتِيَا طَوۡعًا أَوۡ كَرۡهࣰ ا قَالَتَآ أَتَيۡنَا طَآئِعِينَ
41:11.en: Then turned He to the heaven when it was smoke, and said unto it and unto the earth: Come both of you, willingly or loth. They said: We come, obedient

36:38.ar: وَٱلشَّمۡسُ تَجۡرِي لِمُسۡتَقَرࣲّ لَّهَاۚ ذَٰلِكَ تَقۡدِيرُ ٱلۡعَزِيزِ ٱلۡعَلِيمِ
36:38.en: And the sun runneth on unto a resting-place for him. That is the measuring of the Mighty, the Wise

36:39.ar: وَٱلۡقَمَرَ قَدَّرۡنَٰهُ مَنَازِلَ حَتَّىٰ عَادَ كَٱلۡعُرۡجُونِ ٱلۡقَدِيمِ
36:39.en: And for the moon We have appointed mansions till she return like an old shrivelled palm-leaf

36:40.ar: لَا ٱلشَّمۡسُ يَنۢبَغِي لَهَآ أَن تُدۡرِكَ ٱلۡقَمَرَ وَلَا ٱلَّيۡلُ سَابِقُ ٱلنَّهَارِۚ وَكُلࣱّ فِي فَلَكࣲ يَسۡبَحُونَ
36:40.en: It is not for the sun to overtake the moon, nor doth the night outstrip the day. They float each in an orbit

105:1.ar: أَلَمۡ تَرَ كَيۡفَ فَعَلَ رَبُّكَ بِأَصۡحَٰبِ ٱلۡفِيلِ
105:1.en: Hast thou not seen how thy Lord dealt with the owners of the Elephant

105:2.en: Did He not bring their stratagem to naught

105:3.en: And send against them swarms of flying creatures

105:4.en: Which pelted them with stones of baked clay

21:69.ar: قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ
21:69.en: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham

13:15.ar: وَلِلَّهِۤ يَسۡجُدُۤ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ طَوۡعࣰ ا وَكَرۡهࣰ ا وَظِلَٰلُهُم بِٱلۡغُدُوِّ وَٱلۡأٓصَالِ۩
13:15.en: And unto Allah falleth prostrate whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the morning and the evening hours

KKEaKkRj7Pk.speaker: adnan
KKEaKkRj7Pk.speaker_note: Glorious Names series in his voice; refers to verses he recited in the prayer the night before
KKEaKkRj7Pk.title: The Glorious Names of Allah: Al-Qahhar (The Subduer)
KKEaKkRj7Pk.one_line: Al-Qahhar: a name we must not imitate, how Allah subdues all creation, the three ways we are compelled, and why the only thing to subdue is the self.
KKEaKkRj7Pk.summary: Opening the category of correctional control, he explains that Al-Qahhar is unlike names we are asked to emulate: compelling and overpowering belong to Allah alone and the name exists to fill hearts with reverence and turn people from sin. It appears paired only with Al-Wahid because nothing stands beside it. He reads the verses: the Day the earth is replaced and all stand exposed before the One, the Subduer; Yusuf choosing this name when speaking to fellow prisoners, reminding them that the true subduer is not the jailer; the verses that reject partners and the notion of a son; and the angels recording until death. He shows the name in creation, the heavens coming willingly, sun and moon in fixed orbits, and in Allah reversing the nature of things, from water that will burn to the birds against the army of the elephant, the knife that would not cut Isma'il, the fire that would not burn Ibrahim, and Namrud's death by a mosquito. Humans are compelled in three ways: by death, by being given free will that ends on Judgment Day, and by eventual worship that will only count if done now. Islam itself means submission, as in Ibrahim's test and the rites of Hajj. He asks for khashyah, for abandoning the struggle for power over others, and for subduing one's own nafs.

outline.heading: Names of correctional control
outline.gist: This category covers how Allah brings people back from sin and indifference; he chooses Al-Qahhar from it.

outline.heading: A name we must not emulate
outline.gist: Unlike many names we are encouraged to embody, this one exists to instil reverence and fear that move people to leave sin.

outline.heading: Meaning: to subdue, compel and overpower
outline.gist: These words do not fit a servant's conduct; compelling is Allah's role, not ours.

outline.heading: The Day the earth is changed
outline.gist: Everything will be transformed and every person exposed before Allah, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Paired only with Al-Wahid
outline.gist: No other name stands beside it, and on that Day the call will be: whose is the kingdom today? Allah's, the One, the Subduer.

outline.heading: Yusuf in prison: the true Subduer
outline.gist: Unjustly jailed after being thrown in a well, Yusuf reminded his fellow inmates that Allah, not their captors, is the One who subdues all.

outline.heading: Allah created everything; the Prophet only warns
outline.gist: Partners own no harm or benefit; Allah is Creator of all, the One, the Subduer, and no one can claim they were not warned.

outline.heading: Had He wanted a son
outline.gist: The bond between Creator and creation is closer than father and son, since all of us belongs to Him; He is exalted above taking a child.

outline.heading: Subduer over His servants: angels and death
outline.gist: He sends recording angels until death takes the soul, and returns everyone to Him for swift judgment.

outline.heading: The cosmos subdued
outline.gist: The heavens and earth came willingly at His command; sun and moon run their decreed orbits without overtaking one another.

outline.heading: Compelling things to their opposite
outline.gist: Water, the elixir of life, will be made to burn on the Last Day.

outline.heading: The people of the elephant
outline.gist: A few birds carrying pebbles destroyed an army's whole scheme.

outline.heading: The knife, the fire and the mosquito
outline.gist: The knife would not cut Isma'il, the fire would not burn Ibrahim, and Namrud was undone by a mosquito.

outline.heading: First compulsion: death
outline.gist: No one escapes death; it is pure compulsion without oppression, and accepting it early helps one live well.

outline.heading: Second compulsion: the gift of free will
outline.gist: Everything follows its decreed course except humans, whose choice exists only because Allah willed it, and it is withdrawn on Judgment Day.

outline.heading: Third compulsion: everyone will worship
outline.gist: All will eventually pray, love and revere Him; the only question is whether now, when it counts, or after death, when nothing is recorded.

outline.heading: Islam means submission
outline.gist: Islam is surrender, a name taken from Ibrahim, who obeyed the command to sacrifice his son without seeing its wisdom.

outline.heading: Hajj rites as submission
outline.gist: Circling a stone house and throwing pebbles are done because Allah commanded them, whether or not we see the symbolism.

outline.heading: Living the name: khashyah
outline.gist: Reverence combines fear of fair punishment, magnification of His status, and love.

outline.heading: Living the name: do not compel others
outline.gist: Let go of the futile struggle for power; any power should defend the weak, and never coerce an orphan or anyone weaker.

outline.heading: Living the name: subdue your own nafs
outline.gist: The one thing you are meant to overpower is yourself; turning that force on others instead is the worst misuse.

themes.label: The Names and Attributes of Allah
themes.note: Al-Qahhar in the Quran and in creation, and why it is not a name for humans to emulate.

themes.label: Hope, fear and the balance between them
themes.note: Khashyah as fear of just punishment joined to reverence and love.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: Death is the compulsion no one escapes; accepting it improves how one lives.

themes.label: Freedom, rights and responsibility
themes.note: Free will exists only because Allah willed it and ends on Judgment Day.

themes.label: Obedience to Allah and the Messenger
themes.note: Islam as submission, modelled by Ibrahim and enacted in the Hajj rites.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The only legitimate target of compulsion is one's own nafs.

themes.label: Humility vs vanity and arrogance
themes.note: Abandon the struggle for power and never coerce the weak.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Yusuf in prison and Ibrahim with the fire and the knife.

quran.point: The Day the earth and heavens are changed and all appear before the One, the Subduer
Whose is the kingdom today? Allah's, the One, the Subduer
Are many lords better, or Allah, the One, the Subduer
Allah is Creator of all things, the One, the Subduer
I am only a warner; there is no god but Allah, the One, the Subduer
Had Allah wanted a son He would have chosen from His creation
Subduer over His servants, sending guardian angels until death, then swift judgment
He is the Subduer over His servants, the All-Wise, the All-Aware
Heavens and earth told to come willingly or unwillingly; they came willingly
Sun and moon in their orbits, neither overtaking the other
When the seas are set ablaze
The people of the elephant destroyed by birds with stones
The fire made cool and safe for Ibrahim
All in the heavens and earth prostrate willingly or unwillingly

maxims: Compelling is His thing; I'm a servant
Purified coercion, without oppression
His will is for you to have will
You will worship Him; the only question is when
Subdue yourself, not others

stories.who: Yusuf in prison
stories.point: Even when helpless and unjustly confined, remember Allah is the true Subduer

stories.who: The people of the elephant
stories.point: Allah defeats the strongest plots with the smallest creatures

stories.who: Ibrahim, the knife and the fire; Namrud and the mosquito
stories.point: Allah compels things to act against their nature and humbles tyrants

takeaways: Cultivate khashyah: fear of fair punishment, reverence and love together
Accept death as certain and live accordingly
Worship willingly now, while it still counts
Let go of the struggle for power and never coerce those weaker than you
Direct all force toward subduing your own nafs

13:15.ar: وَلِلَّهِۤ يَسۡجُدُۤ مَن فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ طَوۡعࣰ ا وَكَرۡهࣰ ا وَظِلَٰلُهُم بِٱلۡغُدُوِّ وَٱلۡأٓصَالِ۩
13:15.en: And unto Allah falleth prostrate whosoever is in the heavens and the earth, willingly or unwillingly, as do their shadows in the morning and the evening hours

13:16.ar: قُلۡ مَن رَّبُّ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضِ قُلِ ٱللَّهُۚ قُلۡ أَفَٱتَّخَذۡتُم مِّن دُونِهِۦٓ أَوۡلِيَآءَ لَا يَمۡلِكُونَ لِأَنفُسِهِمۡ نَفۡعࣰ ا وَلَا ضَرࣰّ اۚ قُلۡ هَلۡ يَسۡتَوِي ٱلۡأَعۡمَىٰ وَٱلۡبَصِيرُ أَمۡ هَلۡ تَسۡتَوِي ٱلظُّلُمَٰتُ وَٱلنُّورُۗ أَمۡ جَعَلُواْ لِلَّهِ شُرَكَآءَ خَلَقُواْ كَخَلۡقِهِۦ فَتَشَٰبَهَ ٱلۡخَلۡقُ عَلَيۡهِمۡۚ قُلِ ٱللَّهُ خَٰلِقُ كُلِّ شَيۡءࣲ وَهُوَ ٱلۡوَٰحِدُ ٱلۡقَهَّٰرُ
13:16.en: Say (O Muhammad): Who is Lord of the heavens and the earth? Say: Allah. Say: Take ye then (others) beside Him for protectors, which, even for themselves, have neither benefit nor hurt? Say: Is the blind man equal to the seer, or is darkness equal to light? Or assign they unto Allah partners who created the like of His creation so that the creation (which they made and His creation) seemed alike to them? Say: Allah is the Creator of all things, and He is the One, the Almighty

13:17.ar: أَنزَلَ مِنَ ٱلسَّمَآءِ مَآءࣰ فَسَالَتۡ أَوۡدِيَةُۢ بِقَدَرِهَا فَٱحۡتَمَلَ ٱلسَّيۡلُ زَبَدࣰ ا رَّابِيࣰ اۖ وَمِمَّا يُوقِدُونَ عَلَيۡهِ فِي ٱلنَّارِ ٱبۡتِغَآءَ حِلۡيَةٍ أَوۡ مَتَٰعࣲ زَبَدࣱ مِّثۡلُهُۥۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡحَقَّ وَٱلۡبَٰطِلَۚ فَأَمَّا ٱلزَّبَدُ فَيَذۡهَبُ جُفَآءࣰۖ وَأَمَّا مَا يَنفَعُ ٱلنَّاسَ فَيَمۡكُثُ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۚ كَذَٰلِكَ يَضۡرِبُ ٱللَّهُ ٱلۡأَمۡثَالَ
13:17.en: He sendeth down water from the sky, so that valleys flow according to their measure, and the flood beareth (on its surface) swelling foam - from that which they smelt in the fire in order to make ornaments and tools riseth a foam like unto it - thus Allah coineth (the similitude of) the true and the false. Then, as for the foam, it passeth away as scum upon the banks, while, as for that which is of use to mankind, it remaineth in the earth. Thus Allah coineth the similitudes

13:18.ar: لِلَّذِينَ ٱسۡتَجَابُواْ لِرَبِّهِمُ ٱلۡحُسۡنَىٰۚ وَٱلَّذِينَ لَمۡ يَسۡتَجِيبُواْ لَهُۥ لَوۡ أَنَّ لَهُم مَّا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا وَمِثۡلَهُۥ مَعَهُۥ لَٱفۡتَدَوۡاْ بِهِۦٓۚ أُوْلَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمۡ سُوٓءُ ٱلۡحِسَابِ وَمَأۡوَىٰهُمۡ جَهَنَّمُۖ وَبِئۡسَ ٱلۡمِهَادُ
13:18.en: For those who answered Allah's call is bliss; and for those who answered not His call, if they had all that is in the earth, and therewith the like thereof, they would proffer it as ransom. Such will have a woeful reckoning, and their habitation will be hell, a dire abode

2:34.ar: وَإِذۡ قُلۡنَا لِلۡمَلَٰٓئِكَةِ ٱسۡجُدُواْ لِأٓدَمَ فَسَجَدُوٓاْ إِلَّآ إِبۡلِيسَ أَبَىٰ وَٱسۡتَكۡبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ ٱلۡكَٰفِرِينَ
2:34.en: And when We said unto the angels: Prostrate yourselves before Adam, they fell prostrate, all save Iblis. He demurred through pride, and so became a disbeliever

39:67.ar: وَمَا قَدَرُواْ ٱللَّهَ حَقَّ قَدۡرِهِۦ وَٱلۡأَرۡضُ جَمِيعࣰ ا قَبۡضَتُهُۥ يَوۡمَ ٱلۡقِيَٰمَةِ وَٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتُ مَطۡوِيَّٰتُۢ بِيَمِينِهِۦۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ وَتَعَٰلَىٰ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
39:67.en: And they esteem not Allah as He hath the right to be esteemed, when the whole earth is His handful on the Day of Resurrection, and the heavens are rolled in His right hand. Glorified is He and High Exalted from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

9:31.ar: ٱتَّخَذُوٓاْ أَحۡبَارَهُمۡ وَرُهۡبَٰنَهُمۡ أَرۡبَابࣰ ا مِّن دُونِ ٱللَّهِ وَٱلۡمَسِيحَ ٱبۡنَ مَرۡيَمَ وَمَآ أُمِرُوٓاْ إِلَّا لِيَعۡبُدُوٓاْ إِلَٰهࣰ ا وَٰحِدࣰ اۖ لَّآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَۚ سُبۡحَٰنَهُۥ عَمَّا يُشۡرِكُونَ
9:31.en: They have taken as lords beside Allah their rabbis and their monks and the Messiah son of Mary, when they were bidden to worship only One Allah. There is no Allah save Him. Be He Glorified from all that they ascribe as partner (unto Him)

7:138.ar: وَجَٰوَزۡنَا بِبَنِيٓ إِسۡرَٰٓءِيلَ ٱلۡبَحۡرَ فَأَتَوۡاْ عَلَىٰ قَوۡمࣲ يَعۡكُفُونَ عَلَىٰٓ أَصۡنَامࣲ لَّهُمۡۚ قَالُواْ يَٰمُوسَى ٱجۡعَل لَّنَآ إِلَٰهࣰ ا كَمَا لَهُمۡ ءَالِهَةࣱۚ قَالَ إِنَّكُمۡ قَوۡمࣱ تَجۡهَلُونَ
7:138.en: And We brought the Children of Israel across the sea, and they came unto a people who were given up to idols which they had. They said: O Moses! Make for us a god even as they have gods. He said: Lo! ye are a folk who know not

2:255.ar: ٱللَّهُ لَآ إِلَٰهَ إِلَّا هُوَ ٱلۡحَيُّ ٱلۡقَيُّومُۚ لَا تَأۡخُذُهُۥ سِنَةࣱ وَلَا نَوۡمࣱۚ لَّهُۥ مَا فِي ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَمَا فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِۗ مَن ذَا ٱلَّذِي يَشۡفَعُ عِندَهُۥٓ إِلَّا بِإِذۡنِهِۦۚ يَعۡلَمُ مَا بَيۡنَ أَيۡدِيهِمۡ وَمَا خَلۡفَهُمۡۖ وَلَا يُحِيطُونَ بِشَيۡءࣲ مِّنۡ عِلۡمِهِۦٓ إِلَّا بِمَا شَآءَۚ وَسِعَ كُرۡسِيُّهُ ٱلسَّمَٰوَٰتِ وَٱلۡأَرۡضَۖ وَلَا يَـُٔودُهُۥ حِفۡظُهُمَاۚ وَهُوَ ٱلۡعَلِيُّ ٱلۡعَظِيمُ
2:255.en: Allah! There is no deity save Him, the Alive, the Eternal. Neither slumber nor sleep overtaketh Him. Unto Him belongeth whatsoever is in the heavens and whatsoever is in the earth. Who is he that intercedeth with Him save by His leave? He knoweth that which is in front of them and that which is behind them, while they encompass nothing of His knowledge save what He will. His throne includeth the heavens and the earth, and He is never weary of preserving them. He is the Sublime, the Tremendous

70:11.ar: يُبَصَّرُونَهُمۡۚ يَوَدُّ ٱلۡمُجۡرِمُ لَوۡ يَفۡتَدِي مِنۡ عَذَابِ يَوۡمِئِذِۭ بِبَنِيهِ
70:11.en: Though they will be given sight of them. The guilty man will long to be able to ransom himself from the punishment of that day at the price of his children

70:12.en: And his spouse and his brother

70:13.en: And his kin that harboured him

70:14.ar: وَمَن فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ جَمِيعࣰ ا ثُمَّ يُنجِيهِ
70:14.en: And all that are in the earth, if then it might deliver him

TaU4wuBUEso.speaker: adnan
TaU4wuBUEso.speaker_note: continues his own weekend Ramadan Al-Ra'd series and speaks of his role giving fatwas
TaU4wuBUEso.title: Tafsir of Surat Al-Ra'd, Part 4
TaU4wuBUEso.one_line: Explains 13:15-18: all creation prostrates by functioning as commanded, the logic of intermediaries, and the parable of froth over water and gold.
TaU4wuBUEso.summary: He presents haqq as both a value and a law: anything not used with and for it eventually collapses. In 13:15 everything prostrates to Allah, even shadows, and he defines sujud as each thing doing what it was created for: the bird seeking food, the sun on its course, charged particles that physicists can describe but not explain. Our own sujud is lifelong submission through fulfilling our purpose, of which the ritual is one form. Verse 16 exposes the logic of shirk: people want several authorities so they can find easier answers and a middleman to soften the rules, as Bani Israel did with Musa. He warns Muslims against the same: shopping for opinions with no interest in evidence, wanting a fixer, or using the Prophet's intercession as an excuse for low commitment. A mufti offers knowledge, not exemptions, and on contemporary questions each person carries his own choice. Life is short, so use it to know Allah. Verse 17's parable of froth on floodwater and on molten metal shows falsehood rising to the surface and vanishing while what benefits people remains. Hardships are froth too; those who respond to their Lord get the best, while deniers would offer two earths as ransom.

outline.heading: Recap: natural laws and the law of change
outline.gist: The surah first listed constants of creation and placed among them the law that Allah does not change a people until they change.

outline.heading: Haqq as both a value and a law
outline.gist: Allah created everything through haqq, and whatever is not used with and for it eventually fails.

outline.heading: Everything in heaven and earth prostrates
outline.gist: Each creature's sujud is to keep functioning the way Allah commanded it, willingly or unwillingly.

outline.heading: Sujud as submission: the bird and the angels before Adam
outline.gist: A bird seeking food is in sujud; the angels' prostration to Adam was a show of respect in their own form, not our movement.

outline.heading: Even their shadows prostrate
outline.gist: Not only the essence of things but their reflections submit, continuing the image of chasing reflections from the previous verse.

outline.heading: Physics knows how, not why: the elements' submission
outline.gist: Why water stays liquid or like charges repel has no answer beyond 'that is how it is'; that obedience is their sujud.

outline.heading: When everything stops on the Day of Judgment
outline.gist: When Allah folds the heavens and earth and all laws stop, people will realize everything was submitting to Him.

outline.heading: Our sujud is a lifestyle, not only a ritual
outline.gist: Ongoing submission means fulfilling the purpose you were created for; the face on the ground is one form of it.

outline.heading: Who is Lord of the heavens and earth? Allies without power
outline.gist: The allies taken besides Allah cannot bring benefit or harm even to themselves.

outline.heading: The logic of shirk: many authorities, different answers
outline.gist: Multiple authorities only matter if they rule differently; the mushrik wants options so that if one says no another says yes.

outline.heading: Taking scholars as lords: shopping for answers
outline.gist: Seeking whoever says what you want, with no interest in the evidence, borders on what earlier faiths did with their clergy.

outline.heading: The middleman who softens the rules
outline.gist: Across history people wanted someone to excuse them from demanding teachings in exchange for offerings.

outline.heading: Bani Israel: too hard, so give us an idol
outline.gist: They told Musa the commandments were too hard and made the calf as soon as he left, seeking a go-between.

outline.heading: A mufti offers knowledge, not exemptions
outline.gist: In Islam the source is one; on settled ritual questions any recognized opinion is fine, but on contemporary issues each person weighs the evidence and carries the choice.

outline.heading: Everyone wants a guy; prophets were never that guy
outline.gist: Like having a fixer for paperwork, people wanted someone to handle judgment for them; the prophets asked only for time and commitment.

outline.heading: Beware of this in your own mind
outline.gist: Every people drifted this way; the relationship is directly with Allah, and Muslims did the same with intercession.

outline.heading: The Prophet's intercession is by Allah's permission
outline.gist: He saved his accepted dua to intercede for his ummah, but intercedes only for whom Allah permits.

outline.heading: Loving him means emulating his energy
outline.gist: Using intercession to excuse low commitment misreads the story; true love would leave little time for sleep or waste.

outline.heading: Blind and seeing, darkness and light; the one Creator
outline.gist: Rhetorical questions show the states are unequal; Allah created everything, and every supposed partner is His creation.

outline.heading: There was Allah and nothing else: we are shadows
outline.gist: The Prophet's timeless answer to the Yemenis means existence before, after and even now is Allah, and we are here only briefly.

outline.heading: Life is short: an opportunity to know Allah
outline.gist: In his work he sees people die before they can process the news; no one is guaranteed warning or long life.

outline.heading: Blindness as lack of insight
outline.gist: Seeing means understanding what a thing is, where it came from and what it means to you; otherwise it is as if you did not see it.

outline.heading: Floodwater and molten metal both carry froth
outline.gist: Valleys carry water by their capacity and the flow throws up froth; metal melted for jewelry and tools also produces scum.

outline.heading: The parable of haqq and falsehood
outline.gist: Two examples show the pattern is general: the worthless rises to the surface first and is thrown away unnoticed.

outline.heading: What benefits people remains on earth
outline.gist: Water reaches the roots and gold is used; judging by the surface froth leads to every wrong decision.

outline.heading: Falsehood seems to rule the world today
outline.gist: Haqq underlies everything and is stronger; it needs time and people willing to carry it, and then falsehood is forgotten.

outline.heading: Don't abandon the water because of the froth
outline.gist: The Quran is the ultimate haqq that would transform people's lives, but who will deliver it to them remains unsolved.

outline.heading: Those who respond to their Lord get the best; hardship is froth
outline.gist: Sacrifice, rejection and failure sit on top, but the best is what lies beneath.

outline.heading: We remember achievements, not hardships
outline.gist: Dwelling on being cheated or a lost chance is fixating on froth; get up, keep moving, and in Paradise no one recalls the hardships.

outline.heading: Two earths as ransom: possessions are froth
outline.gist: Deniers would give all the earth and another like it; property passes to heirs and strangers who will not care.

outline.heading: Offering family to escape punishment
outline.gist: On seeing Hell people offer children, spouse, siblings and tribe, but not their parents, knowing it would anger Allah further.

outline.heading: The haqq in what you own; which house are you building
outline.gist: The value of possessions is the benefit they bring others and their use as Allah wants; ownership itself means nothing.

themes.label: Relationship with the Quran: reading, reflecting, living it
themes.note: Explains 13:15-18, including the central parable of the surah.

themes.label: Purpose, meaning and the point of life
themes.note: Sujud is each creature fulfilling its function; human sujud is living out the purpose we were made for.

themes.label: Tawhid and worship of Allah alone
themes.note: Shirk seeks multiple authorities and middlemen to soften Allah's demands; the relationship is directly with Him.

themes.label: Jurisprudence rulings and how to approach fiqh
themes.note: Opinion-shopping without regard for evidence is dangerous; a mufti gives knowledge, and people carry their own choices on new issues.

themes.label: Love: of Allah, the Prophet, and one another
themes.note: Love of the Prophet should show in emulating his effort, not in relying on his intercession.

themes.label: Mortality, death and preparing for it
themes.note: We are brief shadows; life can end without warning, so use it to know Allah.

themes.label: Truth and falsehood (haqq and batil)
themes.note: Falsehood is froth that rises first and vanishes; what benefits people stays, so do not be fooled by its apparent dominance.

themes.label: Patience (sabr) and perseverance
themes.note: Hardships are forgotten froth; keep moving after failure and you will see the good beneath.

themes.label: Wealth, asceticism (zuhd), consumerism and money
themes.note: Possessions are froth; their worth lies in benefiting others and using them as Allah wants.

quran.point: The angels' prostration to Adam as a form of respect, not the same movement as ours
Allah folding the heavens and earth on the Day of Judgment
Earlier peoples took their scholars and clergy as lords besides Allah
Bani Israel asking Musa for an idol like other peoples had
No one intercedes with Allah except by His permission
The criminal would ransom himself with his children, spouse, brother and kin

hadith.gist: Every prophet had an accepted dua; the Prophet saved his to intercede for his ummah, prostrating under the Throne on the Day of Judgment
When people of Yemen asked about the beginning, the Prophet said there was Allah and nothing else

maxims: My job is to offer knowledge, not exemptions
Everyone wants a guy; the prophets were never that guy
That's their sujud: doing what they were created for
Falsehood is froth: first on top, first thrown away
What benefits people stays
We're just shadows, here for a little bit

stories.who: Bani Israel and Musa
stories.point: People who found the commandments too hard looked for an idol as a go-between to soften the law.

stories.who: The Prophet's saved dua for intercession
stories.point: His love for his ummah is real, but it works only by Allah's permission and is no excuse for idleness.

contemporary: Seeking a fixer to get paperwork or repairs done, as is common in the Middle East
takeaways: Treat your whole life as sujud by fulfilling the purpose you were created for
Ask for evidence rather than shopping for the answer you want, and own your choices on contemporary issues
Do not use the Prophet's intercession as an excuse for low commitment
Do not be fooled by the apparent dominance of falsehood; hold on to haqq and help bring it to others
After setbacks, keep moving; use what you own to benefit others

20:96.ar: قَالَ بَصُرۡتُ بِمَا لَمۡ يَبۡصُرُواْ بِهِۦ فَقَبَضۡتُ قَبۡضَةࣰ مِّنۡ أَثَرِ ٱلرَّسُولِ فَنَبَذۡتُهَا وَكَذَٰلِكَ سَوَّلَتۡ لِي نَفۡسِي
20:96.en: He said: I perceived what they perceive not, so I seized a handful from the footsteps of the messenger, and then threw it in. Thus my soul commended to me

20:130.ar: فَٱصۡبِرۡ عَلَىٰ مَا يَقُولُونَ وَسَبِّحۡ بِحَمۡدِ رَبِّكَ قَبۡلَ طُلُوعِ ٱلشَّمۡسِ وَقَبۡلَ غُرُوبِهَاۖ وَمِنۡ ءَانَآيِٕ ٱلَّيۡلِ فَسَبِّحۡ وَأَطۡرَافَ ٱلنَّهَارِ لَعَلَّكَ تَرۡضَىٰ
20:130.en: Therefor (O Muhammad), bear with what they say, and celebrate the praise of thy Lord ere the rising of the sun and ere the going down thereof. And glorify Him some hours of the night and at the two ends of the day, that thou mayst find acceptance

21:46.ar: وَلَئِن مَّسَّتۡهُمۡ نَفۡحَةࣱ مِّنۡ عَذَابِ رَبِّكَ لَيَقُولُنَّ يَٰوَيۡلَنَآ إِنَّا كُنَّا ظَٰلِمِينَ
21:46.en: And if a breath of thy Lord's punishment were to touch them, they assuredly would say: Alas for us! Lo! we were wrong-doers

21:69.ar: قُلۡنَا يَٰنَارُ كُونِي بَرۡدࣰ ا وَسَلَٰمًا عَلَىٰٓ إِبۡرَٰهِيمَ
21:69.en: We said: O fire, be coolness and peace for Abraham

22:11.ar: وَمِنَ ٱلنَّاسِ مَن يَعۡبُدُ ٱللَّهَ عَلَىٰ حَرۡفࣲۖ فَإِنۡ أَصَابَهُۥ خَيۡرٌ ٱطۡمَأَنَّ بِهِۦۖ وَإِنۡ أَصَابَتۡهُ فِتۡنَةٌ ٱنقَلَبَ عَلَىٰ وَجۡهِهِۦ خَسِرَ ٱلدُّنۡيَا وَٱلۡأٓخِرَةَۚ ذَٰلِكَ هُوَ ٱلۡخُسۡرَانُ ٱلۡمُبِينُ
22:11.en: And among mankind is he who worshippeth Allah upon a narrow marge so that if good befalleth him he is content therewith, but if a trial befalleth him, he falleth away utterly. He loseth both the world and the Hereafter. That is the sheer loss

22:46.ar: أَفَلَمۡ يَسِيرُواْ فِي ٱلۡأَرۡضِ فَتَكُونَ لَهُمۡ قُلُوبࣱ يَعۡقِلُونَ بِهَآ أَوۡ ءَاذَانࣱ يَسۡمَعُونَ بِهَاۖ فَإِنَّهَا لَا تَعۡمَى ٱلۡأَبۡصَٰرُ وَلَٰكِن تَعۡمَى ٱلۡقُلُوبُ ٱلَّتِي فِي ٱلصُّدُورِ
22:46.en: Have they not travelled in the land, and have they hearts wherewith to feel and ears wherewith to hear? For indeed it is not the eyes that grow blind, but it is the hearts, which are within the bosoms, that grow blind

12:18.ar: وَجَآءُو عَلَىٰ قَمِيصِهِۦ بِدَمࣲ كَذِبࣲۚ قَالَ بَلۡ سَوَّلَتۡ لَكُمۡ أَنفُسُكُمۡ أَمۡرࣰ اۖ فَصَبۡرࣱ جَمِيلࣱۖ وَٱللَّهُ ٱلۡمُسۡتَعَانُ عَلَىٰ مَا تَصِفُونَ
12:18.en: And they came with false blood on his shirt. He said: Nay, but your minds have beguiled you into something. (My course is) comely patience. And Allah it is Whose help is to be sought in that (predicament) which ye describe

20:88.ar: فَأَخۡرَجَ لَهُمۡ عِجۡلࣰ ا جَسَدࣰ ا لَّهُۥ خُوَارࣱ فَقَالُواْ هَٰذَآ إِلَٰهُكُمۡ وَإِلَٰهُ مُوسَىٰ فَنَسِيَ
20:88.en: Then he produced for them a calf, of saffron hue, which gave forth a lowing sound. And they cried: This is your god and the god of Moses, but he hath forgotten

20:89.ar: أَفَلَا يَرَوۡنَ أَلَّا يَرۡجِعُ إِلَيۡهِمۡ قَوۡلࣰ ا وَلَا يَمۡلِكُ لَهُمۡ ضَرࣰّ ا وَلَا نَفۡعࣰ ا
20:89.en: See they not, then, that it returneth no saying unto them and possesseth for them neither hurt nor use

20:85.ar: قَالَ فَإِنَّا قَدۡ فَتَنَّا قَوۡمَكَ مِنۢ بَعۡدِكَ وَأَضَلَّهُمُ ٱلسَّامِرِيُّ
20:85.en: He said: Lo! We have tried thy folk in thine absence, and As-Samiri hath misled them

9:109.ar: أَفَمَنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ تَقۡوَىٰ مِنَ ٱللَّهِ وَرِضۡوَٰنٍ خَيۡرٌ أَم مَّنۡ أَسَّسَ بُنۡيَٰنَهُۥ عَلَىٰ شَفَا جُرُفٍ هَارࣲ فَٱنۡهَارَ بِهِۦ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَۗ وَٱللَّهُ لَا يَهۡدِي ٱلۡقَوۡمَ ٱلظَّٰلِمِينَ
9:109.en: Is he who founded his building upon duty to Allah and His good pleasure better; or he who founded his building on the brink of a crumbling, overhanging precipice so that it toppled with him into the fire of hell? Allah guideth not wrongdoing folk

LTXGRh_gMGM.speaker: adnan
LTXGRh_gMGM.speaker_note: regular Ramadan Quranic Reflections voice; refers to his yearly end-of-Ramadan seven-episode series
LTXGRh_gMGM.title: Ramadan 2024, Night 16: Quranic Reflections on Taha 90 to Al-Hajj 57
LTXGRh_gMGM.one_line: The Samiri and the plots of the nafs, fulfilment through patience and praise, Ibrahim's fire, faith on a cliff edge, and hearts that go blind.
LTXGRh_gMGM.summary: Opening the second half of Ramadan, he recaps the cluster on carrying the message: Al-Anbiya gives the prophets as role models and Al-Hajj frames the mission as a lifelong journey, not a series of milestones. In Taha 96 the Samiri justifies the golden calf as what his soul enticed him to do; he uses this to warn that the nafs dresses self-serving plots as good deeds, and that religious illusions sustain a profitable alliance of clergy and rulers. Taha 130 tells the persecuted Prophet to persevere and glorify Allah day and night so that he may find fulfilment, the one thing people chasing pleasures never reach. Al-Anbiya 46 piles up words of smallness to show that even a breath of punishment would make people confess their wrong. Ibrahim's smashing of the idols teaches that reform must change minds before practices, and the fire made cool shows Allah's command over creation, so calamities test us, not Him. Al-Hajj 11 warns against worshipping on a cliff edge with conditional faith, and Al-Hajj 46 urges learning from history, since it is hearts, not eyes, that go blind.

outline.heading: The second half of Ramadan slips away fast
outline.gist: The second half moves much faster than the first and the nights cascade to the end. Push yourself, revise your plan, hold yourself to it and increase your worship so you have no regrets.

outline.heading: Interlude
Recap: responsibility, pillars, family, fulfilment
outline.gist: The cluster tells Muslims they are responsible for the message, gives Al-Kahf's four pillars against fitnah, names the family as its unit, and shows in Taha that the message brings happiness, not hardship.

outline.heading: Al-Anbiya: the prophets as role models
outline.gist: The surah is named for what it explains: the people you will emulate in carrying the message, what they did, the challenges they faced and their sincerity, ending with the Prophet as the ultimate act of Allah's compassion.

outline.heading: Al-Hajj: carrying the message is a journey
outline.gist: Hajj is a journey of constant movement between holy sites that needs grit, striving, flexibility and decisiveness. Likewise you are asking to be guided to a journey that lasts until the end of your life, not to a fixed point.

outline.heading: Living for points instead of a path
outline.gist: Most people chase milestones: graduation, a job, marriage, a house, a car. Islam says it is a path to walk well, staying on course without deviating.

outline.heading: The end point is Jannah; until then, the path
outline.gist: Milestones exist, but the aim is to stay on the path until Allah lets us cross over Jahannam into Paradise.

outline.heading: The Samiri and the golden calf
outline.gist: Unlike the good Samaritan of the Bible, the Quran's Samiri presented the calf while Musa was away receiving the commandments. Bani Israil, their feet barely dry from the parted sea, worshipped it.

outline.heading: Dust from the hoofprint of Jibril's horse
outline.gist: Musa confronted Harun, who had waited to avoid splitting the people. The reports say the Samiri saw grass spring wherever Jibril's horse stepped and took some of that earth.

outline.heading: 'So my soul enticed me'
outline.gist: Jibril appeared in different forms, and the Samiri was allowed to see him as a test. He cast the earth into a calf of melted gold, which began to low, and at the end blamed his soul's prompting.

outline.heading: Tasweel: a plot laced with lies
outline.gist: The word describes assembling a scheme so complex it is hard to tell truth from falsehood. He found the commandments too rigid and wanted a demigod to give people a way out.

outline.heading: Falling for a phenomenon they didn't understand
outline.gist: Bani Israil were tested by a lowing golden calf called the god of Musa and forgot their reason, though it could neither answer them nor harm or benefit them. The Samiri used something miraculous for a self-serving goal.

outline.heading: The lucrative cycle of clergy and rulers
outline.gist: Idols need offerings that the clergy collect, then the clergy allies with the rulers and everyone profits while people are sold illusions, until a reformist tears them down as Musa did. The story is a test on many levels.

outline.heading: Can you tell sincerity from your nafs' plots?
outline.gist: If you cannot distinguish what is sincere, beneficial and for Allah from what your nafs wants, you are in trouble. The nafs is too clever to propose something openly selfish; it dresses its plots as good.

outline.heading: The Samiri's disguise and his bid for rank
outline.gist: He claimed to be using blessed earth for benefit, but wanted to be the one who gave life to a calf as Musa gave life to a staff. Allah sent Musa back quickly because his people had been led astray, and a few days' delay would have lost them.

outline.heading: Persevere against what they say and glorify your Lord
outline.gist: Revealed during persecution: be patient with what people say to you and about you, and praise Allah before sunrise and before sunset, meaning all through the day.

outline.heading: So that you may find fulfilment
outline.gist: Glorify Him through the night too, so that you may be content. He renders the word as fulfilment: the message is not meant to make you miserable.

outline.heading: The emptiness no milestone fills
outline.gist: True contentment is being at peace with your life, not anxious, depressed and empty after every achievement until the grave.

outline.heading: You've tried everything else; try this
outline.gist: The verse's 'perhaps' reads like an invitation: drugs, alcohol, travel, sex and wealth have not made anyone happier.

outline.heading: Craving meaning but settling for momentary highs
outline.gist: Every human craves a higher reason to exist, but that takes work, so people collect quick highs that leave them miserable whenever they zoom out.

outline.heading: A verse built from words of smallness
outline.gist: A linguistic masterpiece that reduces punishment to almost nothing. He explains the emphatic particle and the conditional 'in', which implies something unlikely to happen.

outline.heading: Massat: the slightest contact
outline.gist: Mass is the most minimal touch, the word used for jinn's influence, which works through whispering: opening catalogues of alternatives until you are confused about what is right.

outline.heading: Nafhah: the very start of a breath
outline.gist: Not even a full puff of air, only its beginning. Each word stacks on the last to shrink the scale further.

outline.heading: The faintest touch and they confess
outline.gist: If the slightest hint of the slightest contact of their Lord's punishment touched them, they would immediately cry woe to us, we were wrongdoers, and want to take everything back.

outline.heading: Young Ibrahim smashes the idols
outline.gist: Ibrahim hoped that toppling the idols would bring people to their senses. They admitted the idols cannot speak and kept worshipping them anyway.

outline.heading: Change the mindset, not just the practice
outline.gist: Modifying practices does nothing if people still think the same way. The ummah needs a change in how it reads the Quran and understands its ethics, values and priorities, or full masajid will make no difference.

outline.heading: The Prophet never toppled an idol in Makkah
outline.gist: In thirteen years neither he nor the companions knocked down an idol; when he returned, he pointed his staff and they fell as people watched. Change the mind and the symptoms fall away.

outline.heading: Thrown into the fire, but Allah commands the fire
outline.gist: A reformist who starts from the wrong end is burned and demonised. But Allah, the Subduer, commands fire to burn as He commands ice to be cold, and it obeys Him.

outline.heading: 'From you, nothing': Allah is my trustee
outline.gist: As Ibrahim flew toward the fire, Jibril asked if he needed anything; he replied that from him he needed nothing, and that Allah was sufficient as his trustee.

outline.heading: O fire, be coolness and peace
outline.gist: He calls it among the most powerful verses in the Quran. Asked later about the best days of his life, Ibrahim named the days inside the fire, cool and peaceful because Allah commanded it.

outline.heading: Calamities test us, not Allah
outline.gist: Seeing oppression and starvation, a Muslim never asks whether Allah can stop it. The question is whether we will put in the effort to feed the hungry, comfort the orphan and save the weak.

outline.heading: Worshipping Allah on a cliff edge
outline.gist: Some worship on the edge: content when good comes, and when trial comes they fall on their faces and lose this world and the next.

outline.heading: Serve Him whether or not you get what you want
outline.gist: Faith conditional on things working out sets you up for failure and disappointment, because life throws painful curveballs whose pain may last a lifetime.

outline.heading: Step back from the cliff
outline.gist: Those who stay only while it is comfortable lose their ethics, values and faith. Trials are coming, so stand far from the edge and build your faith on stable ground, not a crumbling bank.

outline.heading: Commitment is not conditional
outline.gist: Allah sets the conditions, not us. Expecting ease, celebration and instant answers to dua for minimal effort is a delusion.

outline.heading: Travel the earth and learn from history
outline.gist: Muslims are told at least seven times to walk the earth and see how nations rose and fell and what led to it. Read history and watch how the graph moves.

outline.heading: Interlude
Principles reduced to skeletons
outline.gist: When Muslim civilisation prospered its principles were full of meaning; as it fell they became empty shells, such as fasting turned into overeating at night. Those principles must be reclaimed.

outline.heading: Hearts to understand and ears to hear
outline.gist: Walking the earth should give people hearts that absorb the moral of the stories and ears that listen to what happened.

outline.heading: It is the hearts in the chests that go blind
outline.gist: Blindness is a loss of insight, not sight: some blind people see deeply, while some with perfect eyes cannot see what needs reform. Carrying the message needs a heart that can see and learn from those before us.

themes.label: Ramadan: preparation, fasting, making the most of it
themes.note: The second half of Ramadan passes quickly; revise your plan and increase your worship.

themes.label: Stories of earlier prophets
themes.note: Al-Anbiya presents the prophets as the role models for anyone carrying the message.

themes.label: Istiqamah: incorruptibility, steadfastness, moral integrity
themes.note: Guidance is to a lifelong path, like the journey of Hajj, not to a series of milestones.

themes.label: Tazkiyah: purifying and training the self
themes.note: The nafs dresses up self-serving plots as good; one must learn to tell its schemes from sincere action.

themes.label: Reform (islah)
themes.note: Religious illusions keep clergy and rulers profiting until a reformer exposes them.

themes.label: Contentment and acceptance (ridha)
themes.note: Patience with what people say and constant praise of Allah lead to fulfilment, which no worldly pleasure provides.

themes.label: The Hereafter: resurrection, judgment, paradise, hellfire
themes.note: Even the faintest breath of punishment would make people confess their wrongdoing.

themes.label: Reform (islah)
themes.note: Ibrahim and the Prophet show that reform begins with changing how people think; practices follow.

themes.label: Tawakkul: reliance on Allah
themes.note: Ibrahim needed nothing but Allah, who commanded the fire to be cool and peaceful.

themes.label: Trials, hardship and resilience
themes.note: Oppression and calamity in the world test our effort, not Allah's power.

themes.label: Eman: faith, certainty, doubt
themes.note: Faith conditional on comfort sits on a cliff edge; commitment must be unconditional.

themes.label: Islamic history and civilization
themes.note: Learn from the rise and fall of nations; principles hollowed out as civilisation declined, and blind hearts cannot learn.

quran.point: The same expression of the soul enticing someone into a scheme appears in Yaqub's words to his sons.
The calf was called the god of Musa, though it could not answer them or bring harm or benefit.
Allah told Musa his people had been tested after him and led astray by the Samiri.
The image of building on the edge of a crumbling bank, used elsewhere for faith without a stable foundation.

hadith.gist: When the Prophet entered Makkah he pointed at the idols around the Kabah and they fell over.
Ibrahim, when thrown into the fire, said that Allah was sufficient for him and the best disposer of affairs.

maxims: Islam is a journey, not a point
Change the mindset and the symptoms fall
Life is a test for us, not for Allah
Step back from the cliff
You've tried everything else; try this
It's not eyes that go blind, it's hearts

stories.who: The Samiri and the golden calf
stories.point: The nafs builds self-serving schemes and disguises them as blessing; religious illusions are exploited for power and money.

stories.who: Ibrahim smashing the idols
stories.point: Changing practices without changing minds fails; reform starts with how people think.

stories.who: The Prophet and the idols of Makkah
stories.point: He left them standing for thirteen years and they fell on their own once minds had changed.

stories.who: Ibrahim in the fire
stories.point: Total reliance on Allah, who made the fire cool and peaceful; Ibrahim later called those his best days.

contemporary: The search for happiness in drugs, alcohol, travel, sex and wealth
Starvation and oppression in the world prompting people to ask why Allah does not stop it
Religious establishments allied with rulers profiting from people's illusions
Fasting reduced to overeating at night
takeaways: Use the remaining nights of Ramadan: revise your plan and increase your worship.
Question your motives and ask whether an idea is sincere or a plot of your nafs dressed up as good.
Persevere against what people say about you and glorify Allah morning, evening and night to find fulfilment.
When working for reform, change how people think before attacking their practices.
Make your commitment to Allah unconditional and learn from the history of earlier nations.
